title: 第五章　未走之路：新经济政策，1921—1928

他的［布哈林的］传记作者称他为“最后一个布尔什维克”，这个描述是对是错，取决于我们赋予它什么含义。如果我们所说的布尔什维克，是指一个接受新秩序全部原则的人——单一政党的无限权力、党内的“统一”、排斥其他一切意识形态的意识形态、国家的经济专政——并且还相信，在这个框架内可以避免寡头或个人的专制，可以在不使用恐怖的情况下治理，可以保全布尔什维克在夺权斗争中所捍卫的价值：即由劳动人民或无产者治理、自由的文化发展、对艺术、科学和民族传统的尊重——那么，这个描述就是对的。但如果“布尔什维克”意味着这一切，它不过意味着一个无法从自己的前提中得出逻辑结论的人。反之，如果布尔什维克意识形态不只是泛泛而谈，而是包含接受自己原则的必然后果，那么斯大林自夸是所有布尔什维克和列宁主义者中最彻底的一个，就是正确的。

His [Bukharin’s] biographer calls him “the last Bolshevik,” a description which is true or false according to the meaning we attach to it. It is true if we mean by a Bolshevik one who accepted all the principles of the new order—the unlimited power of a single party, “unity” within the party, an ideology excluding all others, the economic dictatorship of the state—and who also believed that it was possible, within this framework, to avoid despotism by an oligarchy or an individual, to govern without the use, of terror, and to preserve the values that the Bolsheviks had championed during the struggle for power: namely, government by the working people or the proletariat, free cultural development, and respect for art, science, and national traditions. But if “Bolshevik” means all this, it simply means a man incapable of drawing logical conclusions from his own premises. If, on the other hand, Bolshevik ideology is not just a matter of generalities but involves accepting the inevitable consequences, of one’s own principles, then Stalin was right to boast himself the most consistent of all Bolsheviks and Leninists.
——莱谢克·科拉科夫斯基，《马克思主义主流》

zh: 布尔什维克刚在内战中获胜，就陷入了新的生存危机。在国际战线上，显然不会有任何世界革命来援助他们；在国内战线上，作为其“基础”的工人和农民不再害怕白卫军，开始背离。于是，经过三年革命，布尔什维克发现自己成了敌对国家中一个被围困的少数派，被一个敌对的世界包围。
en: Hardly had the Bolsheviks prevailed in the Civil War when they were plunged into a new crisis of survival. On the international front it became apparent that no world revolution would come to their aid; on the internal front their worker and peasant “base,” no longer afraid of the Whites, began to defect. So after three years of revolution, the Bolsheviks found themselves a beleaguered minority in a hostile country, surrounded by a hostile world.

zh: 自十月以来，党对世界革命的希望年年高涨，却总在几个月内落空。十月本身的期望在布列斯特-立托夫斯克破灭。1918年底同盟国的崩溃，在次年产生了短暂的巴伐利亚和匈牙利苏维埃共和国，以及作为回应的列宁的共产国际（第三国际）；但西方革命再次没有实现。最大的希望浪潮出现在1920年。在击败白卫军主力之后，当共产国际在莫斯科召开第一次真正代表大会时，苏军向西进发，“越过白色波兰的尸体走向世界革命”。但波兰无产阶级并不想要这种解放，毕苏斯基元帅在华沙城下挡住了苏军。尽管直到1923年仍会有一阵阵德国革命的希望，华沙城下的失败实际上标志着西方革命幻影的终结。此后很清楚，在可预见的未来，无产阶级专政将被困在一个落后的农民国家里。因此，从战时共产主义的千禧年希望中退却，在苏维埃政策的各个方面都成为不可避免。
en: Each year since October the Party’s hopes for world revolution had surged only to be disappointed in a matter of months. The expectations of October itself had been dashed at Brest-Litovsk. The collapse of the Central Powers at the end of 1918 had produced by the following year ephemeral Bavarian and Hungarian Soviet Republics and, in answer, Lenin’s Communist, or Third, International; but again the Western revolution failed to materialize. The greatest surge of hope came in 1920. After the defeat of the main White forces, and while the International was holding its first real Congress in Moscow, Soviet forces headed West “over the corpse of White Poland to world revolution.” But the Polish proletariat desired no such liberation, and Marshal Pilsudski stopped the Soviets at the gates of Warsaw. Although there would be flurries of hope for a German revolution down to 1923, the defeat before Warsaw really marked the end of the Western revolutionary mirage. Thereafter, it was clear that for the foreseeable future the dictatorship of the proletariat would be locked up in a backward, peasant country. Retreat from the millenarian hopes of War Communism therefore became inevitable in every aspect of Soviet policy.

zh: 胜利者的悲哀
en: WOE TO THE VICTORS

zh: 这种期望的降低，首先意味着在一个稳定的国家框架内收缩。1922年后，这个新国家被组织为苏联，在领土上基本上是旧俄罗斯帝国削去部分西部边疆。尽管这种情况并非布尔什维克的本意，它仍被接受为尚未实现的世界苏维埃共和国联盟的替代品；新国家因此按革命方式构建。于是，苏联作为布尔什维克建国年代又一次重大的即兴应对而发展起来——细节上是实验性的，但总体方向是建设党的权力。
en: This lowering of expectations entailed, first, retrenchment within a stable state framework. After 1922, this new state was organized as the Soviet Union, and, in territory, it was essentially the old Russian Empire shorn of some of its western borderlands. Though this situation had not been intended by the Bolsheviks, it was nonetheless accepted as a substitute for the unrealized world union of soviet republics; the new state was accordingly structured in revolutionary fashion. Thus the Soviet Union developed as another of the great Bolshevik improvisations of the founding years—that is, experimental in its details but directed overall to building Party power.

zh: 苏维埃民族政策的起源，在于1917年前对权力的追求。当然，在马克思主义正典中，民族主义不是一种进步力量。但1912年后，列宁至少在暂时策略上支持帝国少数民族的自决权，把它当作反对现存制度的革命力量——正如他同样临时性地支持农民激进主义这一非马克思主义力量。
en: The origins of Soviet nationalities policy lay in the pre-1917 drive for power. Nationalism is, of course, not a progressive force in the Marxist canon. Yet after 1912 Lenin espoused the right to self-determination of the Empire’s minorities, at least on a provisional basis, as a revolutionary force against the existing system—in the same provisional way he espoused the non-Marxist force of peasant radicalism.

zh: 1917年帝国崩溃后，布尔什维克最初的预期是：一旦革命成为世界性的，俄国将不再作为一个单独国家存在，而成为更广泛的社会主义国家联盟的一部分。据此，1918年第一部苏维埃宪法规定了一个向未来新成员开放的联邦，布尔什维克预期帝国获得解放的少数民族将首先加入这个联盟。但这个剧本并不比布尔什维克的世界革命剧本更奏效。1917年的社会主义革命结果严格说来是一件大俄罗斯的事情，所有边疆民族都选择了在“资产阶级”政府下独立。
en: After the Empire collapsed in 1917, the Bolsheviks’ initial expectation had been that once the revolution became worldwide Russia would cease to exist as a separate state and become part of a broader union of socialist countries. Accordingly, the first Soviet constitution in 1918 had provided for a federation open to prospective new members, and the Bolsheviks expected the Empire’s liberated minorities would be the first to join this grouping. But this scenario worked no better than the Bolshevik scenario for world revolution. The socialist Revolution of 1917 turned out to be strictly a Great Russian affair, and all the border nationalities opted for independence under “bourgeois” governments.

zh: 因此，在内战过程中，布尔什维克转向支持无产阶级自决，把它说成比资产阶级独立“更高”的政治形式（正如革命后他们把贫农视为比整个农民阶级“更高”的社会力量）。这项政策意味着大多数边疆国家发生内战，俄国布尔什维克出面干预，支持较弱小的“无产阶级”一方。“白卫”在芬兰和波罗的海国家获胜，这些国家得以独立；但在乌克兰、外高加索以及最终在中亚，红军获胜，这些地区在1920年代初失去独立。苏联正是为容纳这种局面而设计的；这种局面虽然远未达到世界联邦，却仍远不止是族群意义上的俄罗斯。因此，新联盟必须通过采用联邦结构，在形式上向所有成员国的民族自决原则致敬；这还意味着名义上的民族自治和官方使用本地语言，一套俄罗斯帝国从未有过的安排。
en: In the course of the Civil War, therefore, the Bolsheviks shifted to a policy of supporting proletarian self-determination as a “higher” political form than bourgeois independence (just as after the Revolution they viewed the poor peasants as a “higher” social force than the peasantry as a whole). This policy meant civil war in most of the border states, with the Russian Bolsheviks intervening on the weaker, “proletarian” side. The “Whites” won in Finland and the Baltic states, which became independent; but in Ukraine, Transcaucasia, and eventually Central Asia, the Reds triumphed, and those regions lost their independence by the early 1920s. The Soviet Union was devised to accommodate this situation, which, though far short of a world federation, was still much more than ethnic Russia. The new Union, therefore, had to pay formal homage to the principle of national self-determination for all its members by adopting a federal structure, which also entailed nominal ethnic autonomy and the official use of native languages, a set of arrangements that the Russian Empire had never known.

zh: 后来，官方口号变成：各“加盟”共和国“民族形式、社会主义内容”。具体而言，这意味着一种“
”（本土化）政策，即把苏维埃制度“植入”非俄罗斯文化。然而，这个“苏维埃社会主义共和国联盟”与每个“共和国”内的“苏维埃政权”一样，都是虚构，因为在族群门面之后，党在各地都掌握着全面控制权。因此，从1923年获得第一部列宁主义—斯大林主义宪法时起，这个由党征服创建的苏联，始终由一个单一制的党国统治。
en: Later the official slogan came to be that the “constituent” republics were “national in form, but socialist in content.” Concretely, this meant a policy of “

” or the “implantation” of Soviet institutions in the non-Russian cultures. Yet, this “Union” of Soviet Socialist Republics was as much a fiction as was “soviet power” within each of the “republics,” for everywhere behind the ethnic facade the Party was in full control. Thus from the time it received its first, Leninist-Stalinist constitution in 1923, the Soviet Union, created by Party conquest, was always ruled as a unitary Party-state.

zh: 因此，像人们常说的那样，把苏联视为沙皇帝国的简单延续，或视为传统俄国对邻国统治的社会主义伪装延续，是错误的。苏联虽然以自己的方式是一个帝国，却在重大方面与其前身不同。它是一个党帝国，其存在不是为了有限的俄罗斯民族目的，而是为了建设社会主义的国际主义任务。这一使命在它对待少数民族臣民的方式上造成了巨大的实际差别。一方面，它使他们获得作为民族的新尊严；另一方面，又使他们承受为党的目的而遭到大规模动员这种更新、更沉重的奴役——与俄国工人和农民所承受的同样的混合命运。
en: It would therefore he a mistake to view the Soviet Union as a simple continuation of the tsarist empire, as has often been asserted, or as a perpetuation of traditional Russian domination of its neighbors in socialist guise. Though in its own way imperial, the Soviet Union differed in major respects from its predecessor. It was a Party-empire that existed not for circumscribed Russian national purposes but for the internationalist task of building socialism. And this mission made a great practical difference in the way it treated its minority subjects. On the one hand, it raised them to the new dignity of nationhood, and on the other hand it subjected them to the even newer and more onerous servitude of mass mobilization for Party purposes—the same mixed lot that fell to the Russian workers and peasants.

zh: 不过，苏维埃国家这种伪联邦制的伪装也带来危险：少数民族精英可能试图把他们的“自治”变成现实。扶植民族语言、建设共和国政治制度，甚至包括单独的共产党，都为非俄罗斯民族提供了一个发展真正认同的框架。因此，这个不敢自称帝国的帝国的历史，将是“边缘”对“中心”反复挑战、随后莫斯科对共和国进行行政再征服的历史。
en: Still, the Soviet state’s camouflage of pseudofederalism presented the danger that minority elites would try to make their “autonomy” real. The fostering of national languages, the building of republican political institutions, including even separate Communist Parties, gave the non-Russian nationalities a framework in which to develop a genuine identity. Thus the history of this empire that dared not speak its name would be one of recurring challenges by the “periphery” to the “center,” followed by an administrative reconquest of the republics by Moscow.

zh: 然而，内战结束时布尔什维克政权最大的问题，不是世界革命的失败或边疆的重新吸纳，而是一场逼近的国内危机。在苏维埃俄国堡垒内部，党的权力下方突然裂开一道深渊：1921年初，列宁所谓
（工农革命联盟）的两个组成部分——工人和农民——同时开始背离。三月，彼得格勒的罢工升级为喀琅施塔得海军基地的起义。这场运动的驱动力是这样一种信念：军事紧急状态已经结束，人民应当从党手中收回权力。

以“没有共产党人的苏维埃”为口号，这个革命摇篮中的新起义者试图回到1917年公社国家的乌托邦。尽管这个方案现在并不比内战打断它之前更可行，党的回应仍是迄今对其与工人“基础”真实关系最玩世不恭的表明。喀琅施塔得那些僭妄的经验无产者被斥为“白卫分子”和协约国的走狗，并被形而上学无产阶级以军事手段镇压，后者当时正在召开第十次党代表大会。大会中断会议，派出一批代表，由托洛茨基率领，其中包括工人反对派，去攻打要塞并处决头目。但“玩世不恭”也许并不恰当；这些身经百战的布尔什维克真诚地相信，他们遇到的任何敌人，事实上就是人民的敌人。
en: The Bolshevik regime’s greatest problem at the close of the Civil War, however, was not the failure of world revolution or the reabsorption of the borderlands but a looming internal crisis. Within the Soviet Russian bastion itself an abyss suddenly opened beneath the Party’s power: In early 1921 both components of Lenin’s

, the revolutionary alliance of workers and peasants, started to defect simultaneously. In March strikes in Petrograd escalated into a revolt at the naval base at Kronstadt. This movement was driven by the conviction that, with the military emergency over, the people should take back power from the Party.

With the slogan “the soviets without the Communists,” the new insurgents in this cradle of the Revolution sought to return to the 1917 utopia of the commune state. Although this formula could have worked no better now than it had before the Civil War curtailed it, the Party’s response was nonetheless the most cynical indication yet of its real relationship to the worker “base.” The presumptuous empirical proletarians of Kronstadt were denounced as “White Guardists” and lackeys of the Entente, and were put down militarily by the metaphysical proletariat, then assembled for its Tenth Party Congress. The Congress interrupted its sessions to dispatch a cohort of delegates, led by Trotsky and including the Workers’ Opposition, to storm the fortress and execute the ringleaders. But cynical is perhaps not the proper word; these battle-hardened Bolsheviks sincerely believed that any enemy they encountered was ipso facto an enemy of the people.

zh: 与此同时，中部诸省的农民在白卫威胁消除后，也开始骚动反抗。尽管农民对苏维埃治理的执着不如工人，他们的目标本质上相同：收回被没收的革命，通过自己创造的制度管理自己的事务。在这些新的农民暴动中，社会革命党农民亚历山大·安东诺夫领导的坦波夫省起义只是最严重的一起。
党把这些力量斥为“匪帮”，派刚从内战胜利中归来的图哈切夫斯基和布琼尼元帅前去镇压。即便如此，乡村直到1924年才完全置于苏维埃控制之下。
en: At the same time, the peasantry of the central provinces, now that the menace of the Whites had been removed, was stirring in revolt. Although the peasants were less committed to government by soviets than were the workers, their aims were essentially the same: to take back the confiscated Revolution and to manage their affairs through institutions of their own creation. Among these new jacqueries, the insurrection in Tambov province under the leadership of the SR peasant Aleksandr Antonov was only the most serious.

The Party denounced these forces as “bandits” and dispatched Marshals Tukhachevskii and Budennyi, fresh from their victories in the Civil War, to put them down. Even so, the countryside was not brought fully under Soviet control until 1924.

zh: 工人和农民背离的冲击，粗暴地打破了布尔什维克的幻想：他们以为可以继续把战时共产主义当作通往社会主义的捷径。他们突然意识到，自己的政策已使经济陷入毁灭，正如一些孟什维克一直指出的。让我们回想，到1921年，矿场和工厂的产量已降到1913年水平的21%，农业生产降到正常水平的约38%。与此同时，工人阶级几乎消亡：1920年不超过120万人。正如某些孟什维克讽刺的那样，只剩下一个没有无产阶级的专政。
en: The shock of the worker and peasant defections brusquely disabused the Bolsheviks of the illusion that they could continue with War Communism as a quick road to socialism. It was suddenly borne in on them that their policies had brought the economy to ruin, as some Mensheviks had been claiming all along. Let us recall that by 1921 the output of mines and factories had fallen to 21 percent of the 1913 level and that agricultural production was down to about 38 percent of normal. Concurrently, the working class had almost withered away: it numbered no more than 1.2 million in 1920. As certain Mensheviks ironized, there remained only a dictatorship without the proletariat.

zh: 简言之，到1921年第十次党代表大会时，苏维埃政权已濒临崩溃；这不是说有一个有组织的对手准备推翻它——红军已消除了任何此类直接威胁——而是说，如果布尔什维克继续当前路线，国家的人员与物质基础就会在他们脚下解体。当然，一个可能的解决办法是政府召开新的、民主选举的立宪会议，收拾残局，重新开始——就像1871年的法国和1919年的德国在失败政权灭亡后所做的那样。但布尔什维克并不完全处于那种境地；他们遭受了除军事失败以外的一切失败，而且他们从历史逻辑中获得的授权似乎只是被内战的胜利所确认。于是他们坚守权位，硬着头皮把经济政策彻底倒转，从而保全了为社会主义而垄断的权力——这从一开始就是他们存在的理由。
en: In short, by the Tenth Party Congress in 1921 the Soviet regime was near collapse, not in the sense that there was an organized adversary ready to overthrow it—the Red Army had eliminated any such direct threat—but in the; sense that the Bolsheviks could not continue their current course without the human and material fabric of the country disintegrating beneath them. One possible solution, of course, would have been for the government to convene a new, democratically elected Constituent Assembly to pick up the pieces and make a whole new start—as was done in France in 1871 and Germany in 1919, after the demise of failed regimes. But the Bolsheviks were not exactly in that situation; they had suffered every kind of defeat but military, and their mandate from the logic of history seemed only to have been confirmed by victory in the Civil War. So they stayed put and brazened it out by turning their economic policy upside down, thereby saving that monopoly of power for socialism which had been their raison d’être from the start.

zh: 因此，党对1921年危机的回应是双管齐下的。一方面，它向农民和市场作出重大让步，以恢复生产；这种向市场的退却很快被命名为新经济政策（NEP），这个名称最终被用来指整个二十年代。然而另一方面，党收紧党内纪律，加强对全国的政治控制；所以广义上的新经济政策时期，也意味着建设一个“铁板一块”的党和领导权从列宁向斯大林的过渡。
en: Accordingly, the Party’s response to the crisis of 1921 was two-pronged. On the one hand it made significant concessions to the peasants and the market in order to revive production; this retreat to the market was soon baptized the New Economic Policy, or NEP, a designation that eventually would be applied to the entire decade of the twenties. Yet on the other hand the Party tightened discipline within its ranks and strengthened its political control over the country; so the period of the NEP, broadly defined, also means the building of a “monolithic” Party and the transition of leadership from Lenin to Stalin.

zh: 事实上，新经济政策年代既见证了列宁继承人之间的权力斗争，也见证了一场决定他两项政策——经济上的战时共产主义还是狭义的新经济政策——哪一项才是通往社会主义真正道路的较量。在两场较量中，权力斗争更为壮观、更为人熟知，其为人熟知的程度只略逊于1917年的戏剧性事件。因此，这里只简要勾勒，然后再转向新经济政策的经济困境这一更复杂的问题，最后是权力斗争背后更深层的政治进程。
en: In fact, the NEP years saw both a struggle for power among Lenin’s heirs and a contest to determine which of his two policies—economic War Communism or the NEP narrowly defined—was the true road to socialism. Of the two contests the struggle for power is the more spectacular and the better known, indeed only slightly less familiar than the drama of 1917. It will therefore be sketched only briefly here, before moving to the more complex matters of the economic dilemmas of the NEP and, finally, the deeper political processes underlying the struggle for power.

zh: 简言之，对列宁衣钵的争夺，在他开创经济新路线仅一年后就意外展开。1922年，他两次中风，实际上使他脱离权力，直到1924年1月去世。直接结果是政治局的“集体领导”，但人人都预期最终必然出现一位单一领袖。列宁显然的接班人似乎是十月革命的共同缔造者、胜利红军的总司令托洛茨基。正因如此，他的政治局同事——季诺维也夫、加米涅夫和新任党的总书记斯大林——组成“三驾马车”联合反对他。三驾马车与托洛茨基表面上争执的问题，是他对新经济政策的不耐烦，以及由此主张国内快速工业化、国外不断革命。这些“超工业化”观点在1924年第十三次党代表大会上被谴责为“左”倾偏离，从而使托洛茨基退出权力竞争。
en: Briefly, then, the competition for Lenin’s mantle opened unexpectedly only a year after he had inaugurated the new economic course. In 1922, he suffered two strokes that effectively removed him from power until his death in January 1924. “Collective leadership” by the Politburo was the immediate result, but everyone expected that a single chief was bound to emerge. The obvious successor to Lenin appeared to be the coauthor of October and the commander of the victorious Red Army, Trotsky. Precisely for this reason, a “triumvirate” of his Politburo colleagues—Zinoviev, Kamenev, and the newly appointed General Secretary of the Party, Stalin—united against him. The ostensible issue pitting the triumvirs against Trotsky was his impatience with the NEP and consequent advocacy of rapid industrialization at home and permanent revolution abroad. These “super-industrialist” views were condemned as a “Left” deviation at the Thirteenth Party Congress in 1924, thereby removing Trotsky from the competition for power.

zh: 此时，斯大林的三驾马车同伴开始警惕他作为“总书记”、即党机关首脑日益增长的权力。他们也警惕政府在布哈林催促下对农民和市场日益增多的让步，而布哈林此时已是斯大林的政治盟友。于是1925年，季诺维也夫和加米涅夫——几乎没意识到斯大林对机关的控制得多牢——组成了新的“左翼反对派”，并在1925年底第十四次党代表大会上被正式谴责。接着在1926年，他们迟来地与托洛茨基联合，围绕通常的左派对新经济政策的批评组成“联合反对派”；1927年11月，他们在革命十周年之际走上街头，破坏党的纪律，因此被开除出党。
en: At this point, Stalin’s fellow triumvirs became alarmed at

growing power as “Gensek,” or director of the Party apparat. They also became alarmed at the government’s increasing concessions to the peasants and the market at the urging of Bukharin, by now Stalin’s political ally. So in 1925 Zinoviev and Kamenev, little realizing how well Stalin controlled the apparat, formed a new “Left Opposition,” which was duly condemned at the Fourteenth Party Congress at the end of 1925. Then, in 1926, they belatedly joined forces with Trotsky to form a “United Opposition” around the usual Left criticisms of the NEP; and in November 1927 they broke Party discipline by taking to the streets on the tenth anniversary of the Revolution, and so were expelled from its ranks.

zh: 在这个关头，新经济政策的经济措施（我们很快会看到）开始出现问题，斯大林转而采取此前属于左派的纲领。他最近的盟友布哈林，以及布哈林在政治局的盟友——总理阿列克谢·李可夫和工会领袖米哈伊尔·托姆斯基——表示反对，不过与左派不同，他们不敢公开反对。于是1929年，斯大林及其政治局盟友——莫洛托夫、伏罗希洛夫、基洛夫等人——把布哈林派打成“右倾偏离”，剥夺了他们的一切职务。
en: At this juncture the economic programs of the NEP (as we shall see shortly) turned sour and Stalin moved towards what had hitherto been the program of the Left. His recent ally, Bukharin, together with Bukharin’s Politburo allies, Prime Minister Aleksei Rykov and trade union leader Mikhail Tomskii, objected, though unlike the Left, they did not dare to make their opposition public. In 1929, therefore, Stalin and his Politburo allies—Molotov, Voroshilov, Kirov et al.—branded the Bukharinists as a “Right deviation” and deprived them of all their posts.

zh: 这样，二十年代的两个大问题——谁将成为新列宁？哪一种列宁主义政策才是真正的？——最终分别以斯大林获胜和回归战时共产主义告终。在克服一切派别和偏向之后，这位新列宁开始行动，使1929年成为“大转折”之年，成为政权第二次社会主义攻势的开端。
en: Thus, the two great issues of the twenties—Who would be the new Lenin? and Which Leninist policy was the true one?—were decided in favor of Stalin and a return to War Communism. With all factions and deviations overcome, this new Lenin then went into action, making 1929 the Year of the Great Break, the beginning of the regime’s second Socialist Offensive.

zh: 经济困境
en: ECONOMIC DILEMMAS

zh: 然而，那项推动二十年代政治斗争的新经济政策，其性质究竟是什么？进入新政策的第一步，是1921年第十次党代表大会决定以按收成百分比计算的实物税，取代余粮征集制（

）下的强制征粮。更重要的是，农民获得了在自由市场出售余粮的权利。最初，这种出售只允许在地方层面进行，但由于这被证明是一项无法执行的限制，到年底，农产品市场就全面开放了。随着农民通过市场运作，经济其余部分也不得不如此。正如战时共产主义下早先发生的那样，布尔什维克采取了一项他们以为有限的措施，却引发了一个自行发展的进程。然而这一次，他们释放的逻辑不是自己最终纲领的逻辑，而是小资产阶级“投机”的逻辑——一言以蔽之，“资本主义”。
en: What, however, was the nature of that New Economic Policy that had fueled the political struggles of the twenties? The first step into the new policy was the decision, taken at the Tenth Party Congress in 1921, to replace

’s forced requisitions of grain with a tax in kind, calculated as a percentage of the harvest. Even more important, the peasants received the right to sell their surplus production on the free market. Initially, such sales were authorized only at the local level, but since this proved to be an unenforceable restriction, by the end of the year the market for agricultural products became general. And with the peasantry operating through the market, the rest of the economy had to do the same. As occurred earlier under War Communism, the Bolsheviks took what they thought was a limited measure only to fall into a process with an independent momentum. This time, however, the logic they unleashed was not that of their own ultimate program but that of petty bourgeois “speculation”—in a word, “capitalism.”

zh: 很快，市场逻辑渗透到整个经济。货币重新使用，通货得到稳定。于是1924年，对农民的实物税被货币税取代。除了这项税，农民还要按国家确定的价格向国家出售一定比例的收成——这种收购称为
（采购）——其余部分可以在自由市场出售。因此，新经济政策农业中实际上存在两个平行的市场体系。
en: Soon, the logic of the market permeated the whole economy. Money came back into use, and the currency was stabilized. In 1924, therefore, the tax in kind on the peasantry was replaced by a money tax. In addition to this tax, the peasants were expected to sell to the state a percentage of their harvest at prices determined by the state—purchases known as
, or procurements—while the remainder could be sold on the free market. Thus, there in fact existed two parallel market systems in NEP agriculture.

zh: 鉴于经济最大部门——农业——的这种转变，国有工业也必须为市场生产，从而盈利。零售商业和服务业也是如此，它们被直接非国有化。最后，国家预算必须平衡。于是俄国部分回归经济正统。列宁开始告诫他的共产党人“学会经商”，掌握
；这个词通常译为“成本核算”，但更准确的译法是“以盈亏为基础的经营方法”。
en: Given this transformation of the largest sector of the economy—agriculture—state-owned industry, too, had to produce for the market and thus to make a profit. The same was true of retail commerce and services, which were denationalized outright. Finally, the State budget had to be balanced. So Russia made a partial return to economic orthodoxy. Lenin began to exhort his Communists “to learn to trade” and to master
, a term usually translated as “cost accounting” but which is more accurately rendered as “profit-and-loss business methods.”

zh: 因此，到1924年初创始人去世时，苏维埃俄国已发展出一种新颖的混合经济。农业、服务业和小商业被交给私人农民和新的“耐普曼”（nepmen）企业家阶级；但信贷和重工业仍处于社会主义国家控制之下，并被赋予整个体系“制高点”的特权，从而保证不会出现“资本主义复辟”。尽管这一妥协严重偏向国家一方，全国经济仍从内战的恐怖和战时共产主义的灾难中迅速恢复。事实上，到1924年，俄国自1913年以来第一次享有真正的、尽管有限的繁荣。
en: Thus by the Founder’s death at the beginning of 1924, Soviet Russia had developed a novel form of mixed economy. Agriculture, services, and petty commerce were abandoned to private peasants and a new entrepreneurial class of “nepmen”; but credit and heavy industry were kept under the control of the socialist state and privileged as the “commanding heights” of the whole system, thereby guaranteeing there would be no “restoration of capitalism.” Even though this compromise was quite lopsided in favor of the state, the country made a rapid recovery from the horrors of the Civil War and the disasters of War Communism. Indeed, by 1924 Russia enjoyed a genuine, if modest, prosperity for the first time since 1913.

zh: 那么，根本问题就是：新经济政策如何契合一个目标仍是完整社会主义的政权的逻辑？新经济政策是对社会主义梦想的背叛，是对小资产阶级农民和耐普曼投机者的投降，如托洛茨基所暗示的那样吗？还是一场“经济上的布列斯特和约”，一次必要的暂时退却，以便在再次向社会主义前进之前给国家一个“喘息空间”，如列宁似乎所说的那样？抑或它不止是一场布列斯特和约，而实际上是渐进、演化的“长入社会主义”的真正道路，如布哈林最终论证的列宁本意？当然，最后一种立场的一个推论是：斯大林1929年残暴的“大转折”不仅不必要，而且是对真正列宁主义社会主义的背叛。而这个推论的一个推论，则是创始人对他留给党的战时共产主义与新经济政策这两重遗产究竟持什么真实态度的问题。
en: The fundamental question, then, is this: How did the NEP fit into the logic of a regime whose goal remained integral socialism? Was the NEP a betrayal of the socialist dream and a capitulation to the petty bourgeois peasantry and the nepmen speculators, as Trotsky insinuated? Or was it an “economic Brest-Litovsk,” a temporary retreat necessary to give the country a “breathing space” before advancing once again towards socialism, as Lenin seemed to say? Or was it more than a Brest-Litovsk and in fact the true path of a gradual, evolutionary “growing into socialism,” as Bukharin eventually argued was Lenin’s meaning? A corollary to this last position, of course, is that Stalin’s brutal Great Break of 1929 was not only unnecessary but a veritable betrayal of true Leninist socialism. And a corollary to this corollary is the question of the Founder’s real attitude towards the two-headed legacy of War Communism and NEP that he bequeathed to the Party.

zh: 这些问题当时在党内激烈争论，此后在史学中也一直争论。但二十年代的各种立场在后来政治语境中反复出现，其中有一种模式。对于任何相信1930年代苏联终于到达社会主义——无论多么有缺陷——的人来说，新经济政策不是列宁主义的最终结论，至多是一次暂时退却。并非所有持这种看法的人都是斯大林主义者；托洛茨基本人也有同样看法，西方许多社会主义者也一样。但对于那些相信斯大林的方法已损害苏维埃社会主义本身的人来说，新经济政策如果被正确解释为一场逐步超越自身的渐进革命，那才是真正的列宁主义道路，因而也是苏联历史中被错过的重大机会。并非所有持这种看法的人都是列宁主义者；许多人，如约翰·肯尼思·加尔布雷思或早期的安德烈·萨哈罗夫，是社会民主党人或左翼自由派，他们相信一个人道的社会主义苏联有朝一日可能与正在走向社会化的西方趋同。
en: These issues were hotly debated within the Party at the time, and they have been debated in the historiography ever since. But there is a pattern in which the various positions of the 1920s recur in later political contexts. To anyone who believed that the Soviet Union of the 1930s had at last made it to socialism, no matter how flawed, the NEP was not the final word of Leninism but at best a temporary retreat. And not all such people were Stalinists; Trotsky himself shared this view, as have many socialists in the West. But to those who believed that Stalin’s methods had compromised Soviet socialism per se, the NEP, if properly interpreted as a gradualist revolution in the process of transcending itself, was the true Leninist path and, there fore, the great missed opportunity of Soviet history. And not all such people were Leninists; many, such as John Kenneth Galbraith or the early Andrei Sakharov, have been social democrats or left liberals who believed that a humanely socialist Soviet Union could someday converge with a socializing West.

zh: 因此，新经济政策的拥护者从不把它仅仅视为苏维埃过去的一个插曲；相反，他们把它视为斯大林路线之外的永久替代方案，因而也是苏联有朝一日可能回归的模式。事实上，他们在斯大林死后看到了一系列这种回归尝试，即赫鲁晓夫和总理阿列克谢·柯西金时期的各种准市场举措。
当然，戈尔巴乔夫的
本应是最终成功回归新经济政策，从而也是对整个苏联实验的救赎。事实上，有充分理由相信戈尔巴乔夫本人就这样认为，而且他部分是在倾向新经济政策的西方苏联学影响下产生这一想法的。
en: Thus partisans of the NEP never viewed it simply as an episode in the Soviet past; rather, they saw it as a permanent alternative to the Stalinist course, and thus as a model to which the Soviet Union might someday return. Indeed, they saw a series of such attempted returns after Stalin’s death, in various quasi-market initiatives under Khrushchev and Prime Minister Aleksei Kosygin.
Gorbachev’s

, of course, was to have been, at last, the successful return to a neo-NEP and, therefore, the redemption of the Soviet experiment overall. There is in fact good reason to believe that Gorbachev himself thought this, and that he came to this idea in part under the influence of Western. NEP-leaning Sovietology.

zh: 这样，新经济政策就成了判断一个人如何看待苏维埃制度、并进而如何看待社会主义的试金石。斯大林死后的岁月里，公开为他的施政记录辩护变得越来越困难（尽管通过谈论1930年代工业化、城市化和向上社会流动的胜利，仍可能间接辩护；这一点后文再说）。正因如此，在大多数西方著述中，斯大林最终被排除出真正苏联历史的圣典，他的政策和方法被降格为“偏离”。列宁最后几年和布哈林被供奉在他曾经的核心位置，新经济政策则成为苏联历史的核心篇章。于是，那条事实上未被采取的通往苏维埃社会主义的道路，在回溯想象中成了列宁主义的王道。
en: Thus the NEP became the touchstone of what one thought of the Soviet system and, by implication, of socialism. As the years passed after Stalin’s death, it became more and more difficult to defend his record openly (though it remained possible to defend it obliquely by discussing the triumphs of industrialization, urbanization, and upward social mobility in the 1930s; but more on this later). It is for this reason that in most Western writing Stalin was eventually excluded from the canon of true Soviet history, and his policies and methods were demoted to the rank of an “aberration.” In his once central place Lenin’s final years and Bukharin were enshrined, and the NEP became the centerpiece of Soviet history. And so the road to Soviet socialism that was not in fact taken became the royal road of Leninism in retrospective imagination.

zh: 当然，从严格的时间角度看，这很荒谬。斯大林统治的二十五年显然超过新经济政策的八年；如果把战时共产主义三年和勃列日涅夫十八年加到斯大林一边，而把赫鲁晓夫的零碎片段让给新经济政策一边，那么斯大林主义社会主义显然才是苏联历史的经验常态，而新经济政策反而成了“偏离”，或至多是“真正”列宁主义的形而上学常态。再者，如果考虑到斯大林主义的制度影响巨大而持久，而新经济政策的影响很快被抹去，历史账簿两栏的悬殊程度就更不容忽视。因此，考察这种反复出现的新经济政策崇拜时，我们遇到的是苏维埃现实的一种奇怪颠倒。
en: Of course in strictly temporal terms this is absurd, The twenty-five years of Stalin’s rule clearly eclipse the eight years of the NEP; and if one adds to Stalin’s side of the ledger the three years of War Communism and the eighteen of Brezhnev, while conceding bits and pieces of Khrushchev to the side of the NEP, Stalinist socialism is clearly the empirical norm of Soviet history, while it is the NEP that comes out as the “aberration,” or at best as the metaphysical norm of a “real” Leninism. Further, if one takes into account the fact that the institutional impact of Stalinism was enormous and enduring, while that of the NEP was soon obliterated, the disproportion between the two columns of the historical ledger becomes overwhelming. So in approaching the ever-recurring cult of the NEP we encounter a strange inversion of Soviet reality.

zh: 这一崇拜的一位主要倡导者（准确地）将新经济政策视为“苏联马克思主义思想的黄金时代”，并进而把它视为整个苏联实验的黄金时代，一个“多元主义”、“多样性”和“丰富变化”的时期。
这种看法是对是错，取决于人们指的是什么。
en: In the thought of one of the principal celebrants of this cult, the NEP was (accurately) viewed as the “golden era of Marxist thought in the U.S.S.R.” and, by extension, as a golden age of the Soviet experiment
, a period of “pluralism,” “diversity,” and “variety.”
This view is true or false depending on what one means by it.

zh: 如果黄金时代是指苏联历史上人口福祉最好的时期，那么这是对的。用这些经验标准衡量，它显然远好于此前战时共产主义的混乱与贫困，也远好于此后斯大林主义的恐怖与贫困。的确，二十年代中期新经济政策的繁荣，不仅是该国自1913年以来所知的最大繁荣，而且对普通庄稼汉来说，他此后的生活恐怕再也没有如此富足。尽管1913年或1924年令人满意的生活水平与1990年代的标准之间的差异，使这种比较难以量化，但新经济政策时期的生活水平较高，这一判断很有说服力，因为早年显然可以买到食品、人们真正想要的消费品，并且有人身自由。正因如此，新经济政策长期以来在传说中一直是普通俄国人的黄金时代，正如米哈伊尔·佐琴科的故事、伊尔夫和彼得罗夫的小说、谢尔盖·叶赛宁的诗歌或弗拉基米尔·马雅可夫斯基的讽刺剧所描绘的那样。
en: It is true if by golden age one means the best period in Soviet history for the well-being of the population. In these empirical terms it was clearly far better than the chaos and penury of the War Communism that preceded it, or the terror and penury of the Stalinism that followed. Indeed, the prosperity of the NEP of the mid-twenties was not only the greatest the country had known since 1913 but, for the average muzhik, it was probably greater than any he has known since. Although the difference between what constituted a satisfactory standard of living in 1913 or 1924 and what would constitute such a standard in the 1990s makes such a comparison difficult to quantify, the superior living standard of the NEP is eminently plausible with respect to the obvious availability in the earlier years of food, of consumer goods that people actually wanted, and of personal freedom. It is for this reason that the NEP long remained in legend a golden age for ordinary Russians, as in the tales of Mikhail Zosh chenko, the novels of Ilf and Petrov, the poetry of Sergei Esenin, or the satirical plays of Vladimir Maiakovskii.

zh: 但大多数苏联二十年代的颂扬者所说的黄金时代，并不是这个自由随意、追求享乐的新经济政策。在第二种含义中，那个时代之所以是黄金时代，是因为新经济政策的各项政策如果坚持下去，本会通向战时共产主义下未能实现的那种真正社会主义。于是新经济政策成了共产主义发展的“正确”路线。为了判断这一主张的真伪，必须更仔细地考察新经济政策的实际经济记录。
en: But this freewheeling and hedonistic NEP is not what most eulogists of the Soviet twenties mean by golden age. In this second meaning, the time was golden because the policies of the NEP, had they been pursued, would have led to that true socialism which had eluded the regime under War Communism. The NEP thus became the “correct” course for Communist development. In order to judge the truth or falsehood of this claim, it is necessary to look more closely at the NEP’s actual economic record.

zh: 从1921年到1924年，俄国经济在工业品和农产品价格之间经历了剧烈的不均衡摆动，随后才稳定为一个能够运转的体系。1922年，新市场因农产品短缺和工业品过剩而紊乱，导致国家利润骤降。这一局面在1923年的“剪刀差危机”中逆转：农民生产过剩，而工厂压产，从而使农民失去利润，因而失去为城市生产的积极性。然而到1924年，国家通过操纵信贷，压低工业品价格这一刃、抬高农产品价格那一刃，合上了剪刀，稳定了局势。结果，国家有了三个“正常”年份，1924—1926年。这就是所谓的新经济政策的鼎盛期——对一个黄金时代来说并不算长。
en: From 1921 to 1924 the Russian economy went through a wild swing of disequilibrium between industrial and agricultural prices before it stabilized into a functioning system. In 1922 the new market was disrupted by a dearth of agricultural products and a glut of manufactured goods that caused the state’s profits to plummet. This situation was then reversed in the “scissors crisis” of 1923, when the peasants overproduced while the factories held back, thus costing the peasants their profits and, hence, their incentive to produce for the cities. By 1924, however, the state’s manipulation of credit had closed the scissors by forcing the blade of industrial prices down and that of agricultural prices up, thus stabilizing the situation. As a result the country had three “normal” years, 1924-1926. These were the years of what has been called the “High NEP”—not very long for a golden age.

zh: 接着，在1927—1928年冬天，新的危机袭来。在政权看来，问题是另一把看似永久的剪刀正在张开。事实上，贸易条件已变得不利于村庄：农产品价格下跌，而随着国家把生产从轻工业转向重工业，消费品变得稀缺。面对这种“商品荒”，农民进行了政权所谓的“生产罢工”，拒绝按国家确定的价格向国家出售政权为收成规定的粮食定额。相反，农民要么以更高价格在平行的自由市场上卖给耐普曼，要么为国家生产价格更高的经济作物。或者他们把粮食喂给牲畜，然后宰食养肥的牲畜。
en: Then, in the winter of 1927-1928, a new crisis hit. As the regime saw it, the problem was the opening of another, seemingly permanent scissors. And in fact the terms of trade had turned against the village: Agricultural prices fell while consumer goods became scarce as the state shifted production from light to heavy industry. In answer to this “goods famine,” the peasants went on what the regime called a “production strike” by refusing to market at state-determined prices the quotas of grain the regime had set for the harvest. Instead, the peasants chose either to sell to nepmen at higher prices on the parallel free market or to produce higher-priced industrial crops for the state. Or they fed their grain to livestock and then ate the fatted calf.

zh: 使这场“采购危机”在政权看来如此严重的，是它恰逢第一个五年计划的开端；该计划在1927年12月第十五次党代表大会上决定，1928年10月正式启动。到当年夏天，局势已恶化到城市实行配给制；到1929年，农业国俄国居然不得不进口粮食。因此，从实际角度看，到1929年新经济政策已经“失败”——至少从党的观点看是如此。
en: What made this “procurements crisis” so dramatic to the regime was that it coincided with the beginning of the First Five-Year Plan, which had been decided on at the Fifteenth Party Congress in December 1927 and which formally started in October 1928. By the summer of that year, the situation had become so bad that rationing was introduced in the cities; by 1929 agrarian Russia, scandalously, had to import grain. In practical terms, therefore, by 1929 the NEP had “failed”—at least from the Party’s point of view.

zh: 于是，再一次，如同1918年夏天或1921年春天，苏维埃政权发现自己面临生存危机。与1921年一样，这场危机不是以对手直接威胁政权掌权为形式；威胁毋宁是：如果现行政策不变，党的统治所依赖的经济就会崩溃。因此新经济政策的结局与战时共产主义一样：党的政策失败，使党能否继续掌权成了问题。改变方向既必要又紧迫。
en: And so, once again, as in the summer of 1918 or in the spring of 1921, the Soviet regime saw itself confronted by a crisis of survival. As in 1921, this crisis did not take the form of an adversary directly threatening the regime’s hold on power; the threat, rather, was that if existing policies continued unchanged the economy would collapse from under the Party. So the NEP ended as War Communism had: in a failure of Party policy that called into question the continuation of Party power. A change of direction was both imperative and urgent.

zh: 正是在农民与党的计划之间冲突加剧的背景下——尽管情况不尽相同，这一局面仍令人想起内战紧急状态——斯大林领导下的苏联领导层于1929年底放弃新经济政策，选择急转弯，实行强制集体化和冲刺式工业化。这一决定之前，党内进行了一场辩论；布哈林在辩论中反对斯大林，主张调整新经济政策，从而依靠市场和农民走出危机，并为计划筹措资金。这个“布哈林替代方案”正是新经济政策与斯大林主义孰为真正列宁主义这一争论的关键。
en: It was against this background of mounting conflict between the peasantry and the Party’s Plan—a situation reminiscent, mutatis mutandis, of the Civil War emergency—that the Soviet leadership under Stalin abandoned the NEP at the end of 1929 and opted for a brusque switch to forced collectivization and crash industrialization. This decision was preceded by a debate within the Party during which Bukharin argued, against Stalin, in favor of adjusting the NEP and thus of relying on the market and the peasants for a way out of the crisis and for the financing of the Plan. This “Bukharin alternative” is the crux of the controversy over whether the NEP or Stalinism was the true Leninism.

zh: 但为了评估布哈林替代方案的可行性，必须回到苏维埃权力的一些持久悖论。第一个悖论是：一个“无产阶级”政权统治着一个人口绝大多数是农民的国家。我们现在知道，这是马克思主义治理国家的常态，但在当时它似乎是一种反常，是世界颠倒了。列宁似乎颠倒了马克思，正如马克思颠倒了黑格尔；因为世界上第一个胜利的无产阶级政党，最终成了一种悬在空中的“上层建筑”，缺乏完成其社会主义使命所必需的工业“基础”。
en: But in order to assess the feasibility of Bukharin’s alternative it is necessary to return to some enduring paradoxes of Soviet power. The first is that a “proletarian” regime held sway in an overwhelmingly peasant country. We now know this to be the norm in Marxist-governed countries, but at the time it seemed to be an anomaly, the world turned upside down. Lenin seemed to have inverted Marx the way Marx had inverted Hegel, for the world’s first victorious proletarian Party had wound up as a kind of “superstructure” suspended in the air without the necessary industrial “base” to fulfill its socialist mission.

zh: 最初，西方革命本应提供经济援助，帮助俄国渡过这一困境。当这种支持没有出现时，唯一可接受的解决办法，就是党设法为自己的统治建立适当的工业基础。当然，另一个解决办法是承认革命所依据的前提是虚假的，放弃在俄国进行社会主义的整个事业。不用说，在安德烈·普拉东诺夫的《切文古尔》的土地上，对十月的继承者和内战的胜利者来说，这个替代方案毫无吸引力。因此，无论以何种方式，党都执意要设法变出适当的工业基础。由于战时共产主义在这方面已被证明适得其反，1921年之后的问题就是新经济政策能否做到。
en: Initially, the Western revolution was supposed to provide the economic assistance to tide Russia over the duration of this dilemma. When this support failed to materialize, the only acceptable solution was for the Party to somehow generate the appropriate industrial base beneath itself. Another solution, of course, would have been to recognize that the premises on which the Revolution had been based were false and to give up the whole enterprise of socialism in Russia. Needless to say, in the land of Andrei Platonov’s Chevengur, and to the heirs of October and the victors of the Civil War, this alternative lacked appeal. Hence, one way or another, the Party was bent on conjuring up a proper industrial base. Since War Communism had proved counterproductive in this respect, after 1921 the question was whether the NEP could do the trick.

zh: 苏维埃权力的另一个悖论是：与马克思主义理论相反，革命并没有解放充满活力的生产力；相反，它在每一个方面都使国家经济倒退。不仅实际生产在1913年后急剧下降，国家积累的生产资本在七年战争中残破不堪，而且从结构上看，俄国的发展处境也远不如革命前。
en: Another paradox of Soviet power is that the Revolution, contrary to Marxist theory, did not liberate dynamic productive forces; instead it set the country back economically in every respect. Not only did actual production decline drastically after 1913 and the capital stock of the country become dilapidated during seven years of war, but structurally Russia was in a far worse position for development than before the Revolution.

zh: 在旧制度下，俄国是世界市场的一部分：她的货币实行金本位，外国资本大规模投资于她的工业化。的确，在1890年代维特财政大臣任内，她的工业年增长率为8%，世界最高，超过德国和日本。
然而革命后，俄国不再拥有外国投资这一资源。她退出了世界市场，成为一个闭关自守的落后角落，国家小心翼翼地垄断对外贸易。因此，恢复和进一步工业增长，将不得不完全依靠本国资源来实现。
en: Under the Old Regime Russia was a part of the world market: Her currency was on the gold standard, and foreign capital was invested massively in her industrialization. Indeed, in the 1890s under Finance Minister Witte, her annual rate of industrial growth was 8 percent, the highest in the world, surpassing those of both Germany and Japan.

After the Revolution, however, Russia no longer had the resource of foreign investment. She had withdrawn from the world market and become an autarchic backwater in which the state exercised a jealously guarded monopoly of foreign trade. Recovery and further industrial growth, therefore, would have to be engineered entirely out of her own resources.

zh: 但由于革命，俄国的内部状况恶化了。相当一部分“资本家”和知识分子移居国外，留在国内的“资产阶级专家”则作为阶级敌人受到制度性怀疑，沦为二等公民。更重要的是农民地位的变化。革命前，俄国是世界领先的粮食出口国，这一情况为她工业发展赚取了资本。这之所以可能，是因为贵族的大规模生产；此外，使农民不堪重负的税收制度迫使他们到贵族庄园劳动，从而为出口生产。斯托雷平的“押注于强者”造就了一个较富裕的农民阶层（后来被苏维埃称为“富农”），他们也向市场提供余粮。
en: But Russia’s internal situation had worsened because of the Revolution. A good portion of her “capitalists” and intelligentsia had emigrated, and those who remained as “bourgeois specialists” were second-class citizens under institutional suspicion as class enemies. Even more important was the changed status of the peasantry. Before the Revolution Russia was the world’s leading exporter of grain, a circumstance that earned capital for her industrial development. This was possible because of large-scale production by the gentry; in addition, a taxation system that fell heavily on the peasants obliged them to work on gentry estates, and thus for export. And Stolypin’s “wager on the strong” created a class of more prosperous peasants (later called “kulaks” by the Soviets) who also produced a surplus for the market.

zh: 革命把这一切扫荡一空，与其说是通过布尔什维克的行动——他们太弱，做不到这一点——不如说是通过1917—1918年的农民大暴动。

这场暴动消灭了贵族的大地产，迫使富农退回村社，从而消除了俄国农业中能够生产商品余粮的农业生产单位。这种向下拉平也延续了俄国农业的原始性质；特别是，全国仍主要实行三圃制，大多数农民使用木犁。最后，1917年革命把俄国乡村变成了一片由面向自给农业的农户组成的平等主义海洋。革命使这些农户的数量从一千四百万增加到两千五百万。诚然，新经济政策期间出现了新的富农，但他们远未生产出可与革命前相比的可出售余粮。而每当贸易条件不利时，农民因
的经历而对共产党权力长期心存疑虑，干脆退出市场，把他们不多的余粮蒸馏成烈酒。无产阶级专政在乡村几乎没有制度基础或政治影响，除了向农民的需求让步以养活城市工人和红军之外，别无选择。
en: The Revolution swept all this away, not so much through the Bolsheviks’ action—they were too weak for that—as through the great jacquerie of 1917-1918.

This revolt liquidated the large landholdings of the gentry and forced the kulaks back into the commune, thereby eliminating the surplus-producing units of Russian agriculture. This downward levelling also acted to perpetuate the primitive character of Russian agriculture; in particular, the country still operated largely under the three-field system and most peasants used the wooden plow. The Revolution of 1917, finally, transformed the Russian countryside into an egalitarian sea of peasant households oriented towards subsistence farming. The number of these households in creased from fourteen million to twenty-five million as a result of the Revolution. To be sure, new kulaks emerged during the NEP, but they came nowhere near to producing a marketable surplus comparable to what had been available before the Revolution. And whenever the terms of trade were unfavorable, the peasants, chronically suspicious of Communist power because of their experience with

, could simply withdraw from the market and distill their modest surplus into spirits. The dictatorship of the proletariat, having almost no institutional or political presence in the countryside, had little choice but to capitulate to the peasants’ needs in order to keep the workers of the cities and the Red Army fed.

zh: 新经济政策的各项政策不得不在这些国际和国内约束中运作。也正是在这一背景下，必须判断新经济政策为党提供适当工业基础的前景。难怪党内许多人对新政策持怀疑态度。战时共产主义的经济政策在党内几乎得到一致支持，而新经济政策始终引起疑虑并造成分歧。
en: It is within these international and domestic constraints that the policies of the NEP would have to operate. And it is in this context that the prospects of the NEP providing the Party with a proper industrial base must be judged. Small wonder that many in the Party were skeptical of the new policy. Whereas the economic policies of War Communism had enjoyed nearly unanimous support within the Party, the NEP always encountered unease and division.

zh: 起初，在1921—1922年，党内多数人把新经济政策视为不得不作出的艰难选择和被迫退却，有些人则视为社会主义的失败，甚至革命的失败。这一点值得强调，因为它往往被后来对“布哈林替代方案”的热情所掩盖。然而，就实际而言，心怀不满的党接受了新经济政策，因为替代方案将是回到战时共产主义的危险和动荡。因此，正是对不稳定的恐惧，使新经济政策在二十年代余下的时间里占据上风。
en: At first, in 1921-1922, the NEP was viewed by most of the Party as a harsh necessity and a forced retreat, and by some as a defeat of socialism, indeed as the failure of the Revolution. This fact merits emphasis because it has tended to be obscured by later enthusiasm for the “Bukharin alternative.” As a practical matter, however, the disgruntled Party accepted the NEP because the alternative would have been a return to the dangers and turmoil of War Communism. Thus, it was fear of instability that kept the NEP ascendant during the rest of the decade.

zh: 与此同时，党有了第二个谨慎的理由：列宁1922年两次中风；1923年1月之后，他实际上已无法履职，直到十二个月后去世。党就这样失去了那个人：在党存在的每一次危机中，他最终都拿出了“正确”的解决办法。同时，由于继承人之间的斗争不可避免地展开，在这一问题解决之前很难对经济政策作出重大改变，而这一问题要到1927—1928年才告解决。
en: In the meantime the Party was given a second reason for caution when Lenin suffered two strokes in 1922; after January 1923, he was effectively out of action until his death twelve months later. The Party thus lost the man who, in every crisis of its existence, had turned out to have the “right” solution. At the same time, since a struggle for the succession inevitably opened among his presumptive heirs, it was difficult to effect major changes in economic policy until this matter was settled, and that would not happen until 1927-1928.

zh: 正是健康日衰的列宁首先为长期的新经济政策提供了意识形态合理化。他宣称战时共产主义是因军事紧急状态而犯的错误，新经济政策则是回到党最初正确的路线：1918年初的国家资本主义。尽管这并不完全真实——旧形式的国家资本主义意味着容忍大工业家，而新形式意味着容忍小农——它仍为严酷的必需提供了很好的合理化，因为它把新经济政策呈现为通向社会主义的逻辑进程中的一个过渡阶段。因此列宁说，新经济政策是“认真而长期地”采用的，他曾对这段时间作出不同估计，如“不少于十年，可能更长”，但肯定不到二十五年。
en: It was the declining Lenin who first provided ideological rationalizations for a protracted NEP. He declared that War Communism was an error due to the military emergency, and that the NEP was a return to the Party’s initial and correct course: the state capitalism of early 1918. Though this was not really true—the old form of state capitalism had meant tolerating big industrialists, whereas the new form meant tolerating small peasant agriculturalists—it still offered a good rationalization of harsh necessity because it presented the NEP as a transition in a logical process of advancement towards socialism. Lenin therefore stated that the NEP had been adopted “seriously and for a long time,” a span he variously estimated as “not less than a decade, and probably more,” yet certainly under twenty-five years.

zh: 如果这还算含糊，那么过渡的实质就更含糊。随着列宁1922年体力衰退，他对党的告诫显示出对革命悖论性结果的深深困惑。最著名的例证（后文将讨论）是他1922年12月所谓的政治遗嘱，表达了对他身后党的领导层的忧虑。但同样能说明问题的是他1923年1月口授的最后五篇文章，它们常被视为他的经济和社会“遗嘱”。
这些沉思涉及两个担忧。
en: If this was vague, the substance of the transition was vaguer still. As Lenin’s physical powers waned during 1922 his exhortations to the Party revealed deep bafflement about the paradoxical outcome of the Revolution. The best-known illustration of this (to be discussed later) is his so-called political testament of December 1922, which expressed his anxiety about the future leadership of the Party. Yet just as revealing are his last five articles, dictated in January 1923, which have often been treated as his economic and social “testament.”
These ruminations addressed two fears.

children: 〔译注〕列宁年表记载，他的最后文章之一《宁肯少些，但要好些》于1923年2月口授，3月完成并付印。
