zh: 列宁首先处理的，是党和国家机关日益官僚化和腐化的问题——他把这一现象误诊为沙皇制的遗留，而不是新党治本身的后果。为了同官僚化作斗争，他在内战接近尾声时建立了平行的监督官僚机构：针对国家即苏维埃行政的工农检查院，以及针对党的中央监察委员会。这种官僚机构的增殖当然没有奏效，但到1923年初，列宁唯一的解决办法仍然是更多的同类措施：他建议把监察委员会规模扩大一倍，增补工厂一线的诚实工人。
en: Lenin grappled first with the problem of growing bureaucratization and corruption of both the Party and the state apparatus—a phenomenon he misdiagnosed as a holdover from tsarism rather than as a consequence of the new partocracy itself. In order to fight this bureaucratization, toward the end of the Civil War he had created parallel monitoring bureaucracies: the Workers’ and Peasants’ Inspectorate for the state, or Soviet, administration; and the Central Control Commission for the Party. This multiplication of bureaucracies did not work, of course, but Lenin’s only solution by the beginning of 1923 was still more of the same: he recommended a doubling of the size of the Control Commission by the addition of honest proletarians from the factory bench.

zh: 他的第二个担忧，是革命正被“亚洲式”无知和旧俄国的
（大致意为“前文明的”、粗野的或乡野的习俗）所窒息。
为此，他号召党和国家“学习、学习、再学习”。特别是，布尔什维克要拜资产阶级为师，利用它的专家“用非共产党人的手建设共产主义”。换句话说，他们要“通过国家资本主义走向社会主义”。
en: His second fear was that the Revolution was being suffocated by “Asiatic” ignorance and old Russia’s
(approximately: “precivilized,” uncouth, or rustic mores).

To remedy this, he called on the Party and the country to “study, study, study.” In particular, the Bolsheviks were to study at the feet of the bourgeoisie and use its specialists “to build Communism with non-Communist hands.” In other words, they were to move “to socialism through state capitalism.”

zh: 至于与农民至关重要的

，列宁坚持认为，从此以后说服才是把社会主义带到乡村的唯一正确方法。就此他指出，俄国曾经广泛的乡村合作社网络在战时共产主义期间被国有化为分配渠道，如今随新经济政策重新出现；他现在宣称，这些合作社提供了把私人利益与社会主义目的协调起来的手段。但这些新单位将是消费合作社还是生产合作社，他没有说，也没有说明这些合作社如何促进工业化。列宁以这样的断言结束了他的生涯：对俄国来说，“文明合作社社员的制度就是社会主义制度”——这是一个极简主义定义，戈尔巴乔夫在苏维埃主义生命历程末期喜欢反复引用。
en: As for the all-important

with the peasantry, Lenin insisted that henceforth persuasion would be the only correct approach for bringing socialism to the village. And apropos of this, he noted that Russia’s once extensive network of rural cooperatives, which had been nationalized as distribution outlets during War Communism, had re emerged with the NEP; these, he now declared, provided the means to reconcile private interest with socialist purposes. But whether these new units would be consumers’ or producers’ cooperatives he did not say, nor did he offer any hint as to how these cooperatives might contribute to industrialization. And Lenin concluded his career with the assertion that for Russia “a system of civilized cooperators is the system of socialism”—a minimalist definition that Gorbachev was fond of repeating at the end of Sovietism’s life course.

zh: 我们应当如何看待列宁的社会经济遗嘱？这个问题不只是学术性的，因为创始人的话，尤其是他最后日子的话，从此将具有圣经般的权威，不仅在党内争论中，而且奇怪的是，在西方史学中也是如此。无论东方还是西方，都对这位垂危领袖的零碎言论大做文章，因为对一种曾经存在、未来仍会存在的民主列宁主义的信念，正取决于这些话；它们的作用是把战时共产主义放进括号，把苏联实验引向布哈林而不是斯大林的方向。因此，在评价列宁对自己革命的最终评估时，我们实际上面对的是苏联历史上第一条未走之路；因为人们广泛假定，“如果列宁活着”，他肯定不会像斯大林那样对待党或农民。从寿命的统计可能性看，这个问题绝非无聊。列宁去世时只有五十三岁，因此假设他还能活跃十年或更久，确有可能。
en: What should we make of Lenin’s socioeconomic testament? The question is more than academic, for the words of the Founder, and in particular those of his last days, would henceforth carry scriptural authority, not only in intra-Party controversies but, bizarrely, in the Western historiography as well. So much has been made, in both East and West, of the dying Leader’s fragmentary pronouncements be cause on them depends the belief in a once and future democratic Leninism; they serve to put War Communism in parentheses and to point the Soviet experiment in the direction of Bukharin, not Stalin. In evaluating Lenin’s final assessment of his Revolution, therefore, we are in fact dealing with the first of the roads not taken in Soviet history; for the widespread assumption has been that “if Lenin had lived,” he surely would not have acted as Stalin did, either toward the Party or toward the peasants. As an actuarial matter this question is by no means a frivolous one. Lenin was only fifty-three years old when he died, so projecting another decade or more of active life is quite plausible.

zh: 不过，从政治上说，这个问题最好的答案是：延长列宁主义不会带来任何显著差别。真正的选择不是长寿的列宁与斯大林之间，而是迁就农民还是强制农民之间；列宁的合作社是对这个问题的回避。他最后言论的真正意义在于，正是它们的混乱表达了这一困境。正如列宁本人承认的，他把社会主义等同于农民合作社，是回到罗伯特·欧文；欧文一度“浪漫”的纲领，由于俄国阶级斗争的胜利，如今变得现实而正当。
对一位伟大的马克思主义革命家来说，而且面对眼前堆积如山的难题，这个“解决办法”……很可悲。
en: Still, politically, the best answer to this question is that a prolonged Leninism would not have made any notable difference: The real choice was not between a longer-lived Lenin and Stalin, but between accommodating or coercing the peasants; Lenin’s cooperatives were an evasion of this issue. The true significance of his final pronouncements is that their very confusion articulated this dilemma. As Lenin himself admitted, his equation of socialism with peasant cooperatives was a reversion to Robert Owen, whose once “romantic” program had now become realistic and legitimate because of the victorious class struggle in Russia.
For a great Marxist revolutionary, and in view of the staggering problems at hand, this “solution” was … pitiful.

zh: 而且它在相当程度上自相矛盾：列宁对合作社的倡导，实际上被他另外一些更正统马克思主义的声明所否定，那些声明警告乡村中的“私人原则”。因为他最深的信念是：“小生产不断产生资本主义和资产阶级——每天、每小时、自发地、大规模地产生”，
这一观点把村庄视为必须消灭的敌人。但把列宁最后的话奉为神物，最古怪的地方在于这样一种观念：十月革命的最高成就是在1921年之后才发现合作社和市场的美德——而这两者在旧制度下的俄国本来就有。
en: It was, moreover, halfway incoherent: Lenin’s advocacy of cooperatives was in effect negated by other, more authentically Marxist declarations he made warning against the “private principle” in the countryside. For his deepest conviction was that “petty production gives birth to capitalism and the bourgeoisie—continuously, every day, every hour, spontaneously, and on a mass scale,”

a view that stigmatized the village as an enemy to be eliminated. But what is most bizarre in the fetishization of Lenin’s last words is the notion that the supreme achievement of the October Revolution was the discovery, only after 1921, of the virtues of cooperatives and the market—both of which Russia had possessed under the Old Regime.

zh: 如果再加入列宁用更多官僚来治疗党官僚主义的想法，人们得到的印象就是一位被困惑和挫败的领袖，因为革命的结果否定了它最初的前提。即便列宁本人没有看出这一点，也有孟什维克提醒他，甚至声称他的新经济政策不过是在实施他们自己的政策。于是这位病中的领袖不断对这些批评者大发雷霆，因为他内心一定怀疑他们可能说得对。的确，可以合理推测，列宁过早的身体衰退不仅是因为1918年留在他体内的两颗子弹，或糟糕的心血管遗传，而且是因为他革命失望的“躯体化”。
en: If one adds to this Lenin’s notion of curing Party bureaucratism with more bureaucracy, one has the impression of a leader bewildered and frustrated because the outcome of the Revolution had refuted its original premises. And even if Lenin had not been too intelligent to miss seeing this himself, certain of the Mensheviks were there to remind him of it, even claiming that his NEP simply implemented their own policy. So the ailing Leader was in a constant fury with these critics because in his heart he must have suspected that they might be right. Indeed, it is plausible to surmise that Lenin’s premature physical decline was due not just to the two bullets he still had in him from 1918, or to a bad cardiovascular heredity, but to the “somatizing” of his revolutionary disappointment.

zh: 不过，他的各种继承人对于领导革命所负的直接责任较小，会更容易从令人失望的结果中挽救一些东西。这些继承人中的第一个是十月革命的共同缔造者托洛茨基；他的策略是尽可能贴近原初的列宁主义，因此敦促尽早结束新经济政策的退却。
en: His various heirs, however, less directly responsible for leading the Revolution, would find it easier to salvage something from its disappointing results. The first of these heirs was the coauthor of October, Trotsky; his tack was to hew as closely to the original Leninism as was feasible, and hence to urge the earliest possible end to the NEP retreat.

zh: 从1922—1923年开始，托洛茨基警告说，对农民的过度让步才是苏维埃政权的真正危险。他还呼吁发动一场有计划工业发展的新“社会主义攻势”——当然是在准市场框架内——作为保持俄国无产阶级性和进步性的方式。由于他把这一点与如下坚持结合起来：俄国的完整社会主义仍需要较发达国家的一场革命，托洛茨基的总体立场后来被称为“不断革命”。这个标签使他的对手容易声称，他想让俄国革命服从、甚至牺牲于世界革命；于是他们试图把他的立场诋毁为异端的、非列宁主义的“托洛茨基主义”学说。然而事实是，托洛茨基希望把两场革命结合起来。
en: Beginning in 1922-1923, Trotsky warned that excessive concessions to the peasantry were the real danger to Soviet power. He also called for a new “socialist offensive” of planned industrial development—to be sure, within a quasi-market framework—as a way of keeping Russia proletarian and progressive. Because he coupled this with an insistence that full socialism in Russia would still require a revolution in more-developed countries, Trotsky’s overall position came to be known as “permanent revolution.” This label made it easy for his rivals to claim that he wished to subordinate, even sacrifice, the Russian Revolution to world revolution; and thus they sought to discredit his position as the deviant, non-Leninist doctrine of “Trotskyism.” However, the fact is that Trotsky wished to combine the two revolutions.

zh: 但这不是这里的要点，因为俄国几乎无法直接煽动外国革命（尽管并非没有尝试，如1923年德国鲁尔危机期间和1926年中国）。就实际而言，托洛茨基纲领中可操作的部分，是立即在俄国推动有计划工业化，以逐步扭转新经济政策。正如我们所见，正是这个纲领使他和后来的盟友季诺维也夫、加米涅夫在1924年至1927年间被击败。
en: But this is not the point here, for there was little that Russia could do directly to foment foreign revolution (though not for want of trying, as during the Ruhr crisis in Germany in 1923, and in China in 1926). As a practical matter, the operative part of Trotsky’s program was to push for planned industrialization in Russia immediately in order to roll back the NEP. This, as we have seen, was the program on which he and his later allies, Zinoviev and Kamenev, were defeated between 1924 and 1927.

zh: 然而，这个持不同意见的左派最具原创性的理论家，并不是任何大名鼎鼎的政治领袖，而是布哈林当年保卫战时共产主义的合作者叶夫根尼·普列奥布拉任斯基。1924年，普列奥布拉任斯基首次提出他的“社会主义原始积累”理论，作为落后俄国实现工业化的手段。他从马克思那里取来基本范畴，论证一切资本最初都是通过“剥削”和“掠夺”从属的非资本主义群体——如国内农民或外部殖民地——榨取剩余价值而积累起来的。然而俄国别无选择，只能完全依靠国内来源为她发展融资，即依靠作为“内部殖民地”的农民，普列奥布拉任斯基曾轻率地这样称呼。此外，他明确把为俄国社会主义融资与马克思对英国通过圈地进行资本主义原始积累的分析相类比。
en: The most original theorist of this dissenting Left, however, was not any of the big-name political leaders but Bukharin’s erstwhile collaborator in defending War Communism, Evgenii Preobrazhenskii. In 1924 Preobrazhenskii first propounded his theory of “primitive socialist accumulation of capital” as the means by which backward Russia could industrialize. Taking his basic categories from Marx, he argued that all capital was initially accumulated through the expropriation of surplus value through the “exploitation” and “plundering” of subordinate, noncapitalist groups, such as an internal peasantry or external colonies. Russia, however, had no choice but to finance her development from domestic sources alone, that is, from the “internal colony” of the peasantry, as Preobrazhenskii once rashly called it. Moreover, he explicitly drew the parallel between financing socialism in Russia and Marx’s analysis of primitive capitalist accumulation through en closures in England.

zh: 以此类推，俄国的社会主义原始积累将采取把资本从农民“抽送”到国家的形式。这将通过普列奥布拉任斯基所谓的社会主义国家与私人农民生产者之间的“不等价交换”来实现。当然，普列奥布拉任斯基并不主张对农民的榨取采取新战时共产主义的暴力形式。相反，像二十年代所有苏联领导人一样，他坚持乡村的改造必须是和平的、自愿的。因此他论证，对村庄的必要剥削可以通过准市场框架内的财政和金融手段实现。具体而言，这意味着对农民课以不成比例的重税，尤其是由国家采取行动压低农产品价格、同时抬高工业品价格。这样，最大限度的资本就会被抽送到工业扩张中，尤其是重工业和冶金业；计划者现在把这些视为现代性的基石。对于普列奥布拉任斯基和党内多数人来说，扶植工业扩张几乎等同于建设社会主义。
en: By analogy, primitive socialist accumulation in Russia would take the form of “pumping over” capital from the peasantry to the state. This would be achieved by what Preobrazhenskii called “nonequivalent exchange” between the socialist state and the private peasant producer. Preobrazhenskii, of course, did not advocate that this squeeze on the peasantry take the violent form of a new War Communism. On the contrary, like all Soviet leaders in the twenties he insisted that the transformation of the countryside must be pacific and voluntary. Thus he argued that the necessary exploitation of the village could be achieved by fiscal and financial means within a quasi-market framework. Concretely, this meant disproportionate taxation of the peasants and, especially, state action to force agricultural prices down while pushing industrial prices up. In this way the maximum of capital would be pumped over into industrial expansion, especially into heavy industry and metallurgy, now viewed by the planners as the cornerstone of modernity. For Preobrazhenskii, as for most of the Party, fostering industrial expansion had become virtually tantamount to building socialism.

zh: 普列奥布拉任斯基对农业俄国工业化困境的现实评估，在当时的党内斗争中也有政治意义。左派通过强调工业扩张，也把无产阶级、而不是列宁的农民合作社员，置于他们关切的核心。于是他们利用了1921年后持续存在的城市失业这一丑闻，而这一现象是由新经济政策的市场关系造成的。
此外，左派对计划的呼吁，似乎重新点燃了被新经济政策打断的战时共产主义社会主义热情。同时，左派坚持农民农业的自愿改造，加上对党持续官僚化的攻击，似乎充分考虑了列宁最后文章的警告。最后，随着左派在党代表大会上被斯大林机关一次次击败，他们越来越坚决地呼吁党内民主。1930年代之后，这一切被当作一个颇有希望的前景：如果左派赢得权力斗争，他们本会建设出比斯大林所建更人道的社会主义。
en: Preobrazhenskii’s realistic assessment of the dilemmas involved in industrializing peasant Russia also had political significance in the intra-Party struggles of the day. By emphasizing industrial expansion, the Left also made the proletariat, not Lenin’s peasant cooperator, their central concern. Thus they capitalized on the scandal of persistent urban unemployment after 1921, a phenomenon caused by NEP market relations.

The Left’s call for planning, furthermore, seemed to refuel the socialist élan of War Communism that had been broken by the NEP. At the same time, the Left’s insistence on the voluntary transformation of peasant agriculture, in conjunction with its attack on the continuing bureaucratization of the Party, seemed to take full account of the warnings in Lenin’s last articles. Finally, as the Left went from defeat to defeat at the hands of Stalin’s apparat in Party congresses, it called ever more insistently for intra-Party democracy. After the 1930s all of this came to be taken as the fair promise that if the Left had won the struggle for power it would have built a more humane socialism than the one constructed by Stalin.

zh: 这个所谓的左派承诺，一度在许多人看来是苏联历史中被错过的重大机会，后来被称为托洛茨基主义。列宁的政治遗嘱强化了这一信念，因为人们很容易——尽管并不完全准确——把它读成对斯大林的否定和将托洛茨基指定为真正继承人。于是从1930年代到1960年代，托洛茨基主义被视为第二条、也是主要的未走的共产主义道路，是衡量真实苏维埃社会主义的理想替代方案。在它的时代，这一信念产生了第四国际和世界各地形形色色的托派政党。它还激发了伊萨克·多伊彻的文学上的伟大丰碑——关于十月革命的共同缔造者、斯大林的主要对手的马克思主义—弥尔顿式三部曲；在书中，托洛茨基被呈现为先知—受难者，苏联悲剧的真正英雄。这部三部曲还配有一部基本上正面的斯大林传记，毕竟斯大林建设了某种社会主义。
这些著作合在一起，为西方公众提供了可以说是判断苏联经验最有影响力的单一范式。
en: This alleged Left promise, which once appeared to many as the great missed opportunity of Soviet history, came to be known as Trotskyism. This belief was reinforced by use of Lenin’s political testament, which could easily, if not quite accurately, be read as a repudiation of Stalin and an anointing of Trotsky as the true successor. Thus, from the 1930s to the 1960s Trotskyism was deemed the second and principal Communist road not taken, the ideal alternative against which real Soviet socialism would have to be measured. In its day this belief produced a Fourth International and a congeries of Trotskyite parties throughout the world. It also inspired Isaac Deutscher’s great literary monument, his Marxo-Miltonic trilogy on October’s coauthor and Stalin’s archrival, in which Trotsky is presented as a prophet-victim, the true hero of the Soviet tragedy. And this trilogy was supplemented by an essentially positive biography of Stalin, who after all had built a species of socialism.
Together these works have offered the Western public what is arguably the single most influential paradigm for judging the Soviet experience.

zh: 这种托洛茨基主义的苏维埃主义观点，始于这样一个前提：世界第一场社会主义革命在一个落后农民国家中陷入孤立，是一场“意外”；如果西方革命如预期那样实现，它本会来拯救俄国。由于贫穷的俄国无法提供社会主义所需的物质丰裕，工人政党就蜕变成一个半腐化的官僚集团，侵占了国家微薄的资源。于是斯大林主义因而被归结为这一堕落政党的社会学表现。因此，在这种观点中，革命被“背叛”了。但它没有被摧毁——苏维埃俄国仍然是工人国家，因为社会主义的基本纲领已经实现：私有财产已被废除。由此推出，如果斯大林及其爪牙被除掉，制度就能再次繁荣，苏维埃革命最终会变成世界性的。当然，托洛茨基没有活到看见斯大林终结，也没有看见他关于真正社会主义在俄国重生的预言如期应验。但多伊彻比斯大林活得长，他立即开始预言托洛茨基的愿景很快会在赫鲁晓夫的政策中实现。
en: This Trotskyite view of Sovietism begins with the premise that the isolation of the world’s first socialist revolution in a backward peasant country was an “accident”: Had the Western revolution materialized as it was supposed to, it would have come to Russia’s rescue. Because impoverished Russia could not provide the material abundance necessary for socialism, the workers’ Party was transformed into a semi-corrupt bureaucracy that appropriated the country’s meager resources. Stalinism thus was reduced to sociology as the expression of this degenerate Party. So, in this view, the Revolution came to be “betrayed.” But it was not destroyed—Soviet Russia remained a workers’ state because the basic program of socialism had been realized: private property had been abolished. From all of this it followed that if Stalin and his henchmen were removed, the system could flourish once again and the Soviet Revolution would at last become worldwide. Trotsky, of course, did not live to see the end of Stalin and the expected fulfillment of his prophesies of true socialism’s rebirth in Russia. But Deutscher did outlive Stalin, and he immediately began to prophesy that Trotsky’s vision would soon be realized in the policies of Khrushchev.

zh: 不用说，这没有发生。因此，随着时间推移，托洛茨基主义逐渐消退，各托派政党萎缩成微小的宗派。尽管如此，多伊彻所阐述的整个托洛茨基插曲，留下了一份持久的智识残余。首先是这样一种观念：俄国革命的失败或“悲剧”不在于它的列宁主义前提，而在于俄国的落后；如多伊彻所说，是“俄国母亲”败坏了社会主义，而不是社会主义毁了俄国。其推论是：列宁主义社会主义在更有利的条件下本会成功，通常的选择是德国。事实上，更可能的推测是：德国的共产主义革命——或者更准确地说，暂时夺权——会导致内战和经济破坏；这一进程实际上已在1919年巴伐利亚和匈牙利的共产主义起义中开始。在这种情况下，唯一的结果将是把俄国的灾难扩展到欧洲，而不是把俄国从落后中解放出来。
en: Needless to say, this did not happen. Hence, in the course of time Trotskyism faded away, and the various Trotskyite parties dwindled into miniscule sects. Nonetheless, the whole Trotsky episode, as expounded by Deutscher, left an enduring intellectual residue. First, there was the idea that the failure, or “tragedy,” of the Russian Revolution lay not in its Leninist premises but in Russia’s backwardness; as Deutscher put it, it was “Mother Russia” that spoiled socialism, not socialism that ruined Russia. A corollary to this was that a Leninist socialism would have worked under more favorable conditions, the usual choice being in Germany. In fact, a much more likely supposition is that a Communist revolution—or, more exactly, a temporary takeover—in Germany would have led to civil war and economic destruction; indeed, this process actually began during the Communist uprisings of 1919 in Bavaria and Hungary. In such a case the only result would have been to extend the Russian disaster into Europe rather than to liberate Russia from her backwardness.

zh: 尽管如此，这种托洛茨基主义视角的某个版本，主导了西方关于苏维埃俄国的许多写作。这在西方苏联学的第二座伟大纪念碑——E. H. 卡尔的多卷本《布尔什维克革命》——中尤为明显。简言之，这一系列的概念框架是：布尔什维克正在朝着社会主义这一不言自明的现实目标努力，但不利的俄国环境却不断迫使他们偏离适当的社会主义政策。于是，他们把大部分精力用于做保住权力不得不做的事，直到最终驾驭了不听话的原材料，并推进到1929—1930年伟大的“社会主义攻势”，成功奠定了“计划经济的基础”
——这一切归结起来，就是从苏联内部视角讲述的苏联故事，只不过用了更冷静、价值中立的西方语言。但如何最好地把一个国家引向社会主义，并不是一个历史问题；它是一个意识形态和政治问题。
en: Nonetheless, one version or another of this Trotskyite perspective has dominated much of Western writing on Soviet Russia. This is especially apparent in the second great monument of Western Sovietology, E. H. Carr’s multivolume

. Briefly put, the conceptual framework of this series is that the Bolsheviks were working towards the self-evidently realistic goal of socialism, but that they were constantly deflected from appropriate socialist policies by untoward Russian circumstances. Thus, they expended most of their energies doing what they had to do to stay in power, until they finally mastered their recalcitrant raw material and proceeded to the great “socialist offensive” of 1929-1930, which successfully laid the “foundations of a planned economy”

—all of which comes down to the Soviet story told from within a Soviet perspective, though in more sober, value-free Western language. But the question of how best to bring a country to socialism is not a historical question; it is an ideological and political one.

zh: 然而，正是这个问题，成了许多苏联历史经验研究的隐含前提，从而产生了前文讨论过的颠倒史学。而这种颠倒正是托洛茨基范式的本质。因此，那个主题不断重现：革命被“背叛”了——被俄国背叛，被落后背叛，或被斯大林背叛……也就是说，被除革命自身目标之外的一切背叛。当然，其推论是：如果托洛茨基赢了，革命本会顺利发展。因此，在托洛茨基之后很久，他的范式仍会以不同细节、甚至不同“托洛茨基”——例如布哈林或戈尔巴乔夫——回归。
en: Yet it is precisely this question that has been the implicit premise of much of the empirical research on Soviet history, thereby generating the inverted historiography already discussed. And it is this inversion that is the essence of the Trotsky paradigm. So the theme constantly recurs that the Revolution was “betrayed”—betrayed by Russia, or by backwardness, or by Stalin … that is, by everything but the Revolution’s own goals. The corollary to this is, of course, that if Trotsky had won, the Revolution would have worked out all right. Hence, long after Trotsky, his paradigm would return with different details, even with different “Trotskys”—for example, Bukharin or Gorbachev.

zh: 同样，该范式的基本马克思主义也可以被更新，并与现代化理论或年鉴学派的社会史方法相结合。于是，在共产主义崩溃时，该范式的主导形式如下：尽管列宁十月从苏维埃代表大会获得了社会主义“授权”，他的党却不幸因外部世界的敌意而逐渐变成了专政。更大的不幸是，农民俄国使工人政党处于一种不协调的地位，即“悬在空中的先进政治……‘上层建筑’”。于是在斯大林治下，这个上层建筑以强制方式“抢先”在自己下方建立适当“基础”。然而，新社会不可避免地被农民大众迷信而奴性的“心态”以及沙皇专制的威权遗产所“污染”，从而产生了斯大林崇拜这一巨大变形。尽管如此，由于新社会是“工业的、城市的、有教养的”，党的上层建筑最终可以被其发达的基础软化，十月的社会主义授权终将兑现。
托洛茨基、多伊彻和卡尔的观点就这样被不断翻新。
en: Likewise the paradigm’s basic Marxism could be updated and crossbred with modernization theory or the social history methods of the Annales school. Thus, the paradigm’s regnant form at the time of Communism’s collapse ran as follows: Though Lenin received a socialist “mandate” from the Congress of Soviets in October, his Party was unfortunately hardened into a dictatorship by the outside world’s hostility. An even greater misfortune was that peasant Russia left the workers’ Party in the incongruous status of an “advanced political… ‘superstructure’ in the air.” So under Stalin this superstructure coercively “rushed ahead” to build an appropriate “base” beneath itself. Inevitably, however, the new society was “contaminated” by the superstitious and servile “mentality” of the peasant mass, as well as by the authoritarian tsarist heritage, thus generating the great deformation of the Stalin cult. Nonetheless, since the new society was “industrial, urban, and educated,” eventually the Party’s superstructure could be softened by its developed base, and so the socialist mandate of October would at last be made good.
Thus were Trotsky, Deutscher, and Carr constantly recycled.

zh: 同样，那个虚假问题十年又十年地不知疲倦地重现：为什么苏维埃在实现目标时遭遇如此惊人的困难？然而一直以来，正是这些困难本身在呼喊：真正的问题是——当人们试图把一切政治、经济和文化权力集中到一群人手中，以此建设公正人道的社会，追求这一从根本上不可能以这种方式实现的目标时，会发生什么？
en: Thus also, from decade to decade the false question tirelessly re-turned: Why did the Soviets encounter such staggering difficulties in realizing their goal? Yet all along these very difficulties cried out that the true question was: What happens when one tries to realize the intrinsically impossible goal of building a just and humane society by concentrating all political, economic, and cultural power in one set of hands?

zh: 托洛茨基范式的另一个特征，是它设定了每次苏联领导层更替时都会重现的期待；因为每一次继承都激起希望，认为革命终将回到正轨。然而在第一次这样的场合，即斯大林去世时，托洛茨基本人的神话却成了他所开创的综合征的牺牲品。因为赫鲁晓夫的改良主义，加上1960年代西方新左派，产生了第三个斯大林主义之外的理想替代方案：在长寿的列宁和胜利的托洛茨基之后，作为新经济政策鼎盛期的守护人的布哈林，成了指明真正未走之路的人。
en: Another feature of the Trotsky paradigm is that it set the expectations that recurred with every change of Soviet leadership, for with each succession hope surged that the Revolution would at last be put back on track. Yet on the first such occasion, at Stalin’s death, the myth of Trotsky himself fell victim to the very syndrome he had inaugurated. For Khrushchev’s reformism, in conjunction with the Western New Left of the 1960s, produced a third ideal alternative to Stalinism: after a longer-lived Lenin and a victorious Trotsky, Bukharin, as the patron of the High NEP, came to point the true road not taken.

zh: 在这个新视角中，托洛茨基——1920年劳动军事化的倡导者，以及他领导左派时的“超工业化主义者”——逐渐被视为一个失败的斯大林。或者更准确地说，人们逐渐清楚，“斯大林是行动中的托洛茨基”，如莱谢克·科拉科夫斯基所说。科拉科夫斯基继续写道：“多伊彻说……托洛茨基的一生是‘先驱者的悲剧’……但不清楚他究竟是谁的先驱……托洛茨基不是‘先驱’，而是革命的一个分支，在1917—1921年革命所走、后来却不得不放弃的道路上被甩到切线方向……更准确地说，应把他的生命称为追随者的悲剧……。”这段墓志铭最后说：“从来不存在什么托洛茨基主义理论——只有一个被废黜的领袖，他拼命想恢复自己的角色，却无法意识到自己的努力是徒劳的，也不愿为一个他视为奇怪蜕变、但事实上是他与列宁及整个布尔什维克党确立为社会主义基础的那些原则的直接后果的事态承担责任。”
en: In this new perspective, Trotsky, the proponent of the militarization of labor in 1920, and of “superindustrialism” when he was leader of the Left, came to be seen as no more than a failed Stalin. Or more accurately, it gradually became clear that “Stalin was Trotsky

,” as Leszek Kolakowski put it. And Kolakowski continues: “Deutscher says … that Trotsky’s life was ‘the tragedy of the precursor’ … but it is not clear what he is supposed to have been the precursor of…. Trotsky was not a ‘forerunner’ but an offshoot of the revolution, thrown off at a tangent to the course which it had followed in 1917-1921, but which it subsequently had to abandon…. It would be more exact to call his life the tragedy of the epigone….” And this epitaph concludes: “There was never any such thing as a Trotskyist theory—only a deposed leader who tried desperately to recover his role, who could not realize that his efforts were in vain, and who would not accept responsibility for a state of affairs which he regarded as a strange degeneration, but was in fact the direct consequence of the principles that he, together with Lenin and the whole Bolshevik party, had established as the foundations of socialism.”

zh: 这就把我们带到苏联历史中最可信的一条未走之路，因为布哈林对新经济政策的辩护
似乎为托洛茨基和斯大林的政策提供了一个真正的经济替代方案，也比列宁关于合作社的寥寥数语大为改进。布哈林是被普列奥布拉任斯基的社会主义原始积累理论激起这番辩护的；他认为这项政策包含着重返战时共产主义致命冲突的种子，并将终结列宁主义的
；这种看法并非没有道理。
en: This brings us to the most plausible road not taken in Soviet history, for Bukharin’s defense of the NEP

seem to offer a genuine economic alternative to the policies of both Trotsky and Stalin, as well as a considerable improvement upon the meager hints of Lenin about cooperatives. Bukharin was roused to this defense by Preobrazhenskii’s theory of primitive socialist accumulation, which he saw, not incorrectly, as a policy containing the seeds of a return to the lethal strife of War Communism and as the end of the Leninist

zh: 当然，
是一个只存在于党头脑中的虚构。社会阶级既不会自行结盟，也不会自行统治。只有政党组织联盟，而没有任何政党——尤其是现已不存在的左派社会革命党人——曾真正让俄国农民承诺支持列宁的组织。因此，“保全
”现在只是布尔什维克的说法，意思是党再也不能承受攻击农民的代价，否则会削弱政权本身。这正是布哈林面对他所认为的左派新冒险主义时的重大关切。但他也必须考虑左派提出的真实问题，即如何为一个农民国家的工业发展融资。
en: The

, of course, was a fiction that existed only in the mind of the Party. Social classes do not form alliances any more than they rule. Only political parties form alliances, and no political party—especially the now defunct Left SRs—had ever meaningfully committed the Russian peasantry to support of Lenin’s organization. Thus “preservation of the

” was now simply Bolshevik language for saying that the Party could no longer afford to attack the peasantry for fear of undermining the regime itself. And this was Bukharin’s great concern in the face of what he considered to he the Left’s new adventurism. Yet he also had to take account of the real problem raised by the Left, namely, how to finance industrial development in a peasant country.

zh: 于是1925年，布哈林提出了第一个也是唯一一个新经济政策的一般理论。这个理论的基础是这样一种信念：工业增长、因而向社会主义的进步，取决于不断扩大的消费市场，而消费市场又导致农民私人积累。这样，工业扩张的资本就会产生，经济的两大部门——农业和工业——将在“通过交换长入社会主义”的进程中齐头并进。同时，布哈林不得不承认这个进程将是漫长而缓慢的，可能是几十年的事；它将是“蜗牛般速度”的进步，或者像“骑着农民的瘦马进入社会主义”。
en: In 1925, therefore, Bukharin produced the first and only general theory of the NEP. The basis of this theory was a belief that industrial growth, and thus progress towards socialism, depended on an expanding consumer market that, in turn, led to private peasant accumulation. In this way the capital for industrial expansion would be generated, and the two sectors of the economy, agriculture and industry, would move forward in tandem, in a process of “growing into socialism through exchange.” At the same time, Bukharin had to recognize that this process would be protracted and slow, probably a matter of decades; it would be progress “at a snail’s pace,” or like “riding into socialism on a peasant nag.”

zh: 布哈林也承认，这项政策意味着偏向较强、生产率较高的农民，即
的阶级敌人富农。但他没有因此退缩，而是主张进一步扩大新经济政策，使他们也从中受益：1925年，他主张给这些农民无限期租地权和雇佣最多十二名劳工的权利，这些做法此前被谴责为剥削。他甚至大胆地借用七月王朝的资产阶级首相基佐的话，号召农民“发财致富”，这一失言很快不得不收回。
en: Bukharin also recognized that this policy meant favoring the stronger and more productive peasants, those class enemies of the

, the kulaks. Yet he did not shrink from expanding the NEP in their direction: In 1925 he advocated giving these peasants the right to lease land for an indefinite term and to hire up to twelve laborers, practices that had previously been condemned as exploitation. He was even so bold as to summon the peasants—in the words of the bourgeois prime minister of the July Monarchy, Guizot—“to get rich,” a gaffe he quickly had to retract.

zh: 布哈林纲领的要点如下：较强农民及其合作社日益增长的繁荣，将通过税收，以及国家工厂生产他们所需消费品所获得的利润，为国家提供资本；这些资本将允许社会主义工业部门扩张，从而有可能建立模范机械化集体农庄；这些集体农庄将成为较弱农民的磁石；于是随着时间推移，社会主义部门将把私人部门竞争出局；这样，1917—1921年公开的革命阶级斗争将转变为和平的市场竞争，俄国将通过市场“长入社会主义”。这个纲领实际上就是1925—1926年苏联政府的官方政策，即布哈林与斯大林结盟的两年。
en: The Bukharin program’s principal points were these: The growing prosperity of the stronger peasants and their cooperatives would furnish capital to the state, both through their taxes and through the profits of state factories producing consumer goods for their needs; this capital would permit expansion of the socialist industrial sector, thereby making it possible to create model mechanized collective farms; these collectives would serve as magnets for the weaker peasants; thus over time the socialist sector would compete the private sector out of existence; and in this way the open and revolutionary class struggle of 1917-1921 would be transformed into peaceful market competition, and Russia would “grow into socialism” through the market. This program was virtually the official policy of the Soviet government in 1925-1926, the two years of Bukharin’s alliance with Stalin.

zh: 然而应当强调，布哈林的社会主义一旦实现，就毫无混合经济色彩。他的最终目标与其他所有布尔什维克领袖相同：终结私有财产、利润和市场；全面的计划经济；彻底集体化的农业。他的纲领能产生这样的完整社会主义吗？它到底能行得通吗？还是说，它只是马克思主义意识形态分子和各种同路人的市场版切文古尔？
en: Yet it should be emphasized that Bukharin’s socialism, once achieved, would have had nothing of a mixed economy about it. His ultimate goal was the same as that of all the other Bolshevik leaders: the end of private property, profit, and the market; a fully planned economy; and a wholly collectivized agriculture. Could his program have produced such an integral socialism? Could it have worked at all? Or was it only market Chevengur for Marxist ideologues and assorted fellow travellers?

zh: 为了回答这些问题，必须更仔细地考察1927年后瓦解新经济政策的危机的性质。到那一年，俄国经济实际上已完成革命后的恢复，农业产量恢复到战前约90%，工业产量恢复到约75%。但这只是经济重建中容易的部分。国家起点如此之低，进步只能迅速，增长率相应很高。此外，手头的任务是把现有工业设备重新运转起来，这需要相对较少的资本支出。
en: In order to answer these questions it is necessary to look more closely at the nature of the crisis that undermined the NEP after 1927. By that year the Russian economy had virtually completed its post-Revolutionary recovery and had returned to some 90 percent of prewar agricultural production and some 75 percent of industrial production. But this was the easy part of economic reconstruction. The country had started from so low a level that progress could only be swift and growth rates correspondingly high. Moreover, the task at hand had been to put an existing industrial plant back into operation, and this had required a relatively low outlay of capital.

zh: 然而到1927年，任务是翻新和更换日益过时、自1913年以来没有得到新投资的工业设备。无论什么样的政府统治俄国，无论它是否旨在建设社会主义，这样的努力都是必需的。而这种努力将吸收巨额资本。由于这些资金不能像沙皇时代那样来自国外，资本将不得不越来越多地从面向国内消费市场的生产转向重工业投资。这意味着，无论如何，工业化都将以农民为代价来融资——正如普列奥布拉任斯基所论证的那样。正是农民不愿按这些条件生产，导致了1927年底袭击政权的“采购危机”，并随着计划启动而逐年加深。因此，1927年政权面临的结构性困境是：它别无选择，只能加快工业化；但这样做又必然使它失去农民的支持。
en: By 1927, however, the task was to refurbish and replace an increasingly obsolete industrial plant that had received no new investment since 1913. Such an effort would have been required no matter what kind of government ruled Russia and whether or not it aimed to build socialism. And this effort would have absorbed very large sums of capital. Since these sums could not come from abroad, as under tsarism, capital would have to be shifted increasingly from production for the domestic consumer market to investment in heavy industry. This meant that, one way or another, industrialization would be financed on the backs of the peasants—just as Preobrazhenskii had argued. It was the peasants’ reluctance to produce on these terms that led to the “procurements crisis” that hit the regime at the end of 1927 and deepened each year thereafter as the Plan swung into action. Thus the structural dilemma facing the regime in 1927 was this: It had no choice but to industrialize more rapidly, yet if it did so, it would inevitably alienate the peasantry.

zh: 但共产党人为什么不能更好地让农民继续生产呢？毕竟新经济政策正是为此设计的，本应有可能再次调整政策，消除新的剪刀差。原因在于，新经济政策事实上从来不是后来人们以为的混合经济。它一直只是一个勉强被容忍的准市场，不断受到国家事无巨细的干扰。
en: But why could not the Communists have done better at keeping the peasants producing? The NEP, after all, had been designed for just this purpose, and it should have been possible to adjust the policy once again to eliminate the new scissors. The reason is that the NEP in fact had never been the mixed economy it was later taken to be. It had never been more than a barely tolerated quasi-market subject to constant and minute harassment from the state.

zh: 首先，战时共产主义的基本制度在1921年后并没有拆除。最高国民经济委员会及其所有
仍然存在，继续监管仍属国有的经济“制高点”，尽管许多工厂现在拥有有限自主权，可以通过组织成生产“托拉斯”和销售“辛迪加”来实行
。国家银行恢复，并获得近乎垄断的信贷权；它按党的命令收紧或放松信贷。国家计划委员会也仍然存在。事实上，它现在开始了真正的生涯：1923年后，它开始发布生产“控制数字”或预测，并为将来恢复社会主义攻势的那一天拟订越来越详细的计划。自然，这个组织已成为左派和那些毕竟选择支持社会主义政权的孟什维克的基地。所有这些制度都产生了一种国家干预的惯性，在整个新经济政策期间有增无减。
en: First of all, the basic institutions of War Communism had not been dismantled after 1921. Vesenkha, with all its
, was still there, and it continued to oversee the still nationalized “commanding heights” of the economy, even though many factories now had a limited autonomy to pursue

by organizing themselves into production “trusts” and marketing “syndicates.” The State Bank was revived and given a near monopoly of credit, which it turned up or down at the behest of the Party. And Gosplan, too, was still there. Indeed, it now began its real career: After 1923 it started issuing “control figures,” or forecasts, for production and drafting increasingly detailed plans for the day when the socialist offensive would be resumed. Naturally, this organization had become a base for the Left and for Mensheviks who rallied to what was, after all, a socialist regime. And all of these institutions generated a statist momentum that continued unabated throughout the NEP.

zh: 与此同时，约80%的非农业经济仍属国有。因此，城市私人部门只包括小零售商业、小手工业、边缘信贷机构和少数不大的工厂。最重要的是，这个私人部门由形形色色的中间商组成，各种中间人在国家分配体系的缝隙中活动，搜罗稀缺商品，以高于国家价格出售。这些就是耐普曼，被政权污名为“投机者”，常常遭到民众怨恨，但如果没有他们，就根本不会有市场。农民当然构成了私人部门的其余部分；这里所谓的村庄霸主是富农，另一个“剥削者”，因此是阶级敌人。
en: At the same time, some 80 percent of the nonagricultural economy remained nationalized. Thus the urban private sector consisted only of small retail commerce, petty artisan manufacture, marginal institutions of credit, and a few modest factories. Above all, this private sector consisted of a great variety of middlemen, intermediaries of all sorts who operated in the interstices of the state distribution system to scrounge up scarce goods to sell at higher than state prices. These were the nepmen, stigmatized by the regime as “speculators” and often resented by the population, yet necessary if there were to be a market at all. The peasantry, of course, made up the rest of the private sector; here the alleged lord of the village was the kulak, another “exploiter” and, as such, a class enemy.

zh: 显然，这个由耐普曼和富农组成的私人部门，蜷缩在“制高点”的阴影下，而政权明确要最终消灭这一部门，它，根本无法与党的社会主义部门匹敌。我们在这里面对的，也不是任何可识别意义上的混合经济，无论是以社会民主主义的斯堪的纳维亚模式，还是国家社团主义的日本模式。
en: Clearly, this private sector of nepmen and kulaks, huddling in the shadow of the “commanding heights” and explicitly destined by the regime for eventual liquidation, was no match for the Party’s socialist sector. Nor are we dealing here with a mixed economy in any recognizable sense of that term, whether in the mode of Social Democratic Scandinavia or state-corporate Japan.

zh: 在这些情况下，新经济政策的俄国，党从未按市场规则玩经济游戏，这几乎毫不奇怪。相反，它的主要管理方法用布尔什维克的行话说，是“行政的”，意思是政治命令或直接强制。诚然，所有政府都在某种程度上干预市场运作，但苏联政府在二十年代的干预是持续的、无处不在的，而且最重要的是反复无常的。这不是“意外”，也不是领导人迟钝所造成的结果。这些干预的原因一律是政治性的，即通过打击所谓的敌对阶级来支撑党的权力，即便这损害了商品的实际生产和分配。
en: Given these circumstances, it is hardly surprising that in NEP Russia the Party never played the economic game according to market rules. Rather, its principal method of management was, in Bolshevik jargon, “administrative,” by which was meant political fiat or outright coercion. To be sure, all governments intervene to some degree in the operations of the market, but the Soviet government’s interventions during the twenties were constant, ubiquitous, and above all capricious. And this was no “accident” or the result of obtuse leadership. The cause of these interventions was uniformly political, namely, to bolster Party power by combatting allegedly hostile social classes, even though this hurt the real production and distribution of goods.

zh: 于是，耐普曼被课税、管制，甚至以“投机”罪名逮捕，尽管他们能把消费品带到国家“辛迪加”无法到达的村庄，或者在官方
不到位时，以高于国家收购价的价格收购农民粮食再在城市转售。
结果，耐普曼人数在二十年代后半期稳步下降，市场在这个所谓混合经济中的角色也相应萎缩。同样，生产能力强而富裕的富农被过度征税和管制，从而减少了他们的生产，扰乱了国家采购。
en: Thus the nepmen were taxed, regulated, and indeed arrested for “speculation,” despite the fact that they brought consumer goods to the villages when state “syndicates” could not, or that they bought up peasant grain at higher than state prices for resale in the cities when official
were not forthcoming.

Consequently, the number of nepmen steadily declined in the second half of the decade, and the role of the market in the national economy correspondingly dwindled in this supposedly mixed economy. Similarly, the productive and prosperous kulaks were overtaxed and overregulated, thus decreasing their production and disrupting state procurements.

zh: 换句话说，1927年的危机不是市场机制失灵或生产能力下降意义上的

危机。只要换到他们想要的东西，农民就有能力也愿意生产余粮，但新经济政策市场在国家压力下的枯萎，阻止了任何这样的等价交换。因为1927年2月之后，党越来越多地干预以提高工业品价格，以减少农民需求对投资的压力，同时压低采购价格，使国家能更便宜地获得粮食。原因当然是计划工业化作为无产阶级政权基础所享有的政治和意识形态优先地位。但结果与维持新经济政策不相容。正如我们长期研究这一问题的权威所说：“［1927年］选择的［价格］政策，基本上敌视工业、贸易和农业中的市场力量。要么必须修改政策，要么必须摧毁市场及其表现。”
简言之，问题不是富农，而是党。因此，二十年代末的危机是
危机，它将在1929年的大转折中得到政治解决。
en: In other words, the crisis of 1927 was not an

crisis in the sense of a failure of market mechanisms or a decline of productive capacity. The peasants were able and willing to produce a surplus if they received something they wanted in exchange, but the withering of the NEP market under state pressure prevented any such equivalent exchange. For after February 1927 the Party increasingly intervened to raise industrial prices in order to reduce the pressure of peasant demand on investment, while simultaneously lowering procurement prices in order to make food cheaper for the state. The reason, of course, was the political and ideological priority accorded to planned industrialization as the base for a proletarian regime. But the result was incompatible with maintaining the NEP. As our longest-running authority has put the matter: “The [pricing] policy chosen [in 1927] was basically hostile to market forces in industry, trade, and agriculture. Either the policy would have to be amended, or the market and its manifestations would have to be destroyed.”
In short, the problem was not the kulaks, it was the Party. Thus, the crisis of the end of the decade was
, and it would receive a political solution in the Great Break of 1929.

zh: 此外，政权对市场施压的心理效果，是使民众对接下来可能发生什么始终不确定。这只会加深对苏维埃政权的不信任，尤其是在乡村，那里由于战时共产主义的经历，猜疑本来就很深。在这种情况下，民众几乎没有积极性去积累任何东西，更不用说把积累所得投入政权的社会主义建设——于是既挫败了普列奥布拉任斯基的期望，也挫败了布哈林的期望。
en: Moreover, the psychological effect of regime pressure on the market was to keep the population in constant uncertainty about what might come next. This only fostered distrust of Soviet power, especially in the villages, where suspicion was already deep owing to War Communism. Under such circumstances, the population had little incentive to accumulate anything, and still less to invest it in the regime’s socialism—thus confounding the expectations of both Preobrazhenskii and Bukharin.

zh: 正是在这种情况下，1927年布哈林调整了他原来的新经济政策理论，以考虑即将到来的计划的需要；这个修订后的理论就是所谓的布哈林替代方案。

暂且不论它在更理想情况下是否可行，我们可以注意到，在当时的情况下，它在很大程度上是一种损害控制。因为从本质上说，他朝普列奥布拉任斯基和左派的方向移动，同意国家应当使用“某种挤压”来从农民那里提取工业化资本；但他坚持这应当缓慢而谨慎地进行。当1928年情况更加艰难时，他甚至允许“一点点”强制也许是合适的，但没有说明“一点点”是多少。因此，他的纲领代表的是节奏上的差异，而不是［方向］上的差异。换句话说，他诉诸的是布尔什维克
（行政干预）的较温和版本，而不是朝着市场方向深化新经济政策。除此之外，他主张增加粮食进口，以帮助城市度过
的低谷。
en: It was under these circumstances that in 1927 Bukharin adapted his original theory of the NEP to take account of the exigencies of the forthcoming Plan; and it is this revised theory that is known as the Bukharin alternative.

Leaving aside for the moment the question of its feasibility under more ideal circumstances, we may note that in the situation at the time it was largely an effort at damage control. For in essence he moved in the direction of Preobrazhenskii and the Left by agreeing that the state should use “some squeeze” in order to extract from the peasants the capital for industrialization; he insisted, however, that this should be done slowly and cautiously. And when the going got rougher still in 1928, he even allowed that “a little” coercion might be in order, but without specifying how much was “a little.” His program thus represented a difference in tempo more than in In other words, he resorted to a softer version of Bolshevik
, not to a deepening of the NEP in the direction of the market. For the rest, he advocated that grain imports should be increased to tide the cities over the slack in

zh: 很难看出这些措施如何在现有局势中造成实质性差别，因为政权在1927—1928年面临两个基本事实。第一，对农民的

压力都只会使采购危机更糟——毕竟，农民在1927年“商品荒”之后立即减少了销售。第二，政权既然计划已经启动，就承受不起缓慢解决这个问题。在这种关头，直接押注于［市场］——这本应是新经济政策的真正逻辑——将需要无法预测的时间，却不能保证任何可预测的量化结果。因此，这种赌博风险太大，不能考虑，布哈林甚至从未建议过。所以，作为对新经济政策软性行政挤压的真正替代，只剩下战时共产主义那种对农民的人身强制。而这正是斯大林1929年最终采取的道路。
en: It is difficult to see how these measures could have made a substantial difference in the existing situation, for the regime was confronted with two basic facts in 1927-1928. One was that

pressure on the peasants would only make the procurements crisis worse—after all, the peasants had reduced marketing immediately following the “goods famine” of 1927. The second was that the regime, with its Plan already under way, could not afford a slow solution to this problem. At such a juncture, an outright wager on the would have been the true logic of the NEP—would have taken an unpredictable length of time without guaranteeing any predictable quantitative results. Such a gamble was therefore far too risky to contemplate, and Bukharin never even suggested it. So as a real alternative to the soft administrative squeeze of the NEP there remained only physical coercion of the peasants in the manner of War Communism. And this was the course finally adopted by Stalin in 1929.

zh: 但这种路线选择不只是斯大林个人的任性，也不是如果在新经济政策最后日子里由更明智、更温和或更“列宁主义”的领导人掌舵就可以避免的判断错误。问题不在司机，而在车辆。党不是一辆可以套上农民瘦马、拉着走过落后乡村几十年才抵达社会主义的车辆。党被创造出来是为了领导和战斗，为了冲击阶级敌人，强行推动历史进程。一场布列斯特和约，无论是外交的还是经济的，都只是为新的攻势积蓄力量的策略。而到二十年代末，党已拥有这种力量。新经济政策年代伟大的“社会”事实，就是列宁的党成熟为一个更新类型的组织：一台真正的战争机器，用来完成被1921年退却所中断的对俄国的征服。
en: But this choice of route was not just Stalin’s personal caprice, nor an error in judgment that could have been avoided if wiser, or softer, or more “Leninist,” leaders had been at the wheel of the Party during the NEP’s final days. The problem was not with the driver but with the vehicle. The Party was not a machine to be harnessed to some peasant nag and drawn for decades through the backward countryside before reaching socialism. The Party had been created to lead and to fight, to charge the class enemy and to force the hand of history. A Brest-Litovsk, whether diplomatic or economic, was only a strategem to gather strength for a new offensive. And by the end of the twenties the Party had this strength. The great “social” fact of the NEP years was the maturation of Lenin’s Party into an organization of a still newer type: an authentic war machine to complete the conquest of Russia interrupted by the retreat of 1921.

zh: 政治解决
en: POLITICAL SOLUTIONS

zh: 这一发展的关键在1921年第十次党代表大会上给出，当时列宁明确表示，经济上的新经济政策不会带来政治上的新经济政策。相反，党内纪律被收紧，党对国家的控制被加强。其背后的逻辑是布尔什维主义熟悉的军事逻辑：党被围困在一个敌对的国家和敌对的世界中，其队伍中的任何裂缝都会使异见者“客观上”成为国内敌对势力和外部帝国主义阵营的代理人。这确实是喀琅施塔得的教训。
en: The key to this development was given in 1921 when, at the Tenth Party Congress, Lenin made it clear that the economic NEP would not entail a political NEP. On the contrary, discipline within the Party was tightened and the Party’s control over the country was strengthened. The logic behind this was the familiar military one for Bolshevism: with the Party besieged in a hostile country and in a hostile world, any fissure in its ranks would make the dissidents “objectively” the agents of enemy forces within the country and in the camp of imperialism outside it. This, indeed, had been the lesson of Kronstadt.

zh: 因此，党内纪律通过禁止“派别”并以开除作为派别活动的惩罚而得到保障。

党内仅存的民主是“民主集中制”，其含义是在任何重大决定之前进行非派别讨论，此后服从新的党的路线。于是“党的铁板一块的统一”原则得以确立。诚然，禁止派别在二十年代实践中并未完全遵守，但党发展的持续趋势是消灭派别，到1929年它们全部消失。因此，托洛茨基和其他后来声称禁令本应只是临时措施的人，对此事采取了一种表面的形式主义看法。事实上，这种禁令合乎逻辑地源自《怎么办？》中所概述的党的结构；托洛茨基本人1903年就承认了这一点，当时他宣称，在列宁的安排中，“党的机关取代了［普通党员］，中央委员会取代了党的机关，最后，一个‘独裁者’取代了中央委员会。”
en: Intra-Party discipline was therefore insured by banning “factions” and making expulsion the penalty for factional activity.

The only democracy that now remained in the Party was “democratic centralism,” which meant nonfactional discussion before any major decision and then conformity with the new Party line thereafter. Thus was established the principle of the “monolithic unity of the Party.” To be sure, the ban on factions was not observed in practice during the 1920s, but the constant tendency of the Party’s development was towards the elimination of factions, and by 1929 they were all gone. Thus Trotsky and others who later alleged that the ban was to have been only temporary took a superficially formalistic view of the matter. In fact, such a ban followed logically from the structure of the Party as outlined in

; Trotsky himself had acknowledged this in 1903 when he declared that in Lenin’s scheme of things “the Party apparatus is substituted for the [rank and file], the Central Committee is substituted for the Party apparatus, and finally a ‘dictator’ is substituted for the Central Committee.”

zh: 与此同时，列宁拧紧了对国家的政治控制。这通过1922年苏联历史上头两场公审完成。一场针对社会革命党人，列宁最初想枪毙他们；但在外国社会民主党人的说情下，他们只被流放到西伯利亚。另一场针对孟什维克，同样为了安抚西方舆论，他们只是被驱逐到西方。这样，一党制国家中最后一些政治异类被清除了。
en: Concurrently, Lenin tightened the screws of political control over the country. This was done in 1922 with the first two show trials in Soviet history. One was for the SRs, whom Lenin initially wanted to shoot; but on the intercession of foreign Social Democrats they were only exiled to Siberia. The other was for the Mensheviks, who—again in order to mollify Western opinion—were simply expelled to the West. Thus the last political anomalies were removed from the one-Party state.

zh: 同时，党扩大了，内部也收紧了。到1929年，党经历了四个发展阶段。1917年之前，它是一个由专职革命者组成的地下组织——事实上是一个密谋团体，目标是如果沙皇政权被推翻就夺取政权。1917年，它短暂地成为一个群众性政党，或至少是一个拥有群众追随者的政党，尽管其领导层仍致力于密谋夺权。战时共产主义期间，党成为一个国家机构，通过一个无所不能、遍及各处的苏维埃官僚体系进行统治或试图统治，并通过双重管理控制这个体系。但由于大多数党员忙于战争的紧急任务，党在这一时期未能稳定其治理角色。只是在1921年之后，党才最终定型为持久的国家行政机关，一个稳定的党国。
en: At the same time, the Party was expanded and tightened internally. As of 1929 the Party had gone through four phases of development. Until 1917 it was an underground organization—in fact a conspiracy—of full-time revolutionaries whose goal was to come to power if the tsarist regime were ever overthrown. In 1917 it briefly became a mass party, or at least a party with a mass following, though its leadership remained committed to a conspiratorial seizure of power. During War Communism the Party became a state institution that ruled, or tried to rule, through an omnicompetent and universal Soviet bureaucracy, one that it controlled through the dual administration. But because most of its membership was preoccupied with the emergency task of war, the Party was unable to stabilize in its governing role during this period. It was only after 1921 that the Party assumed its final form as an enduring state administration, a settled Party-state.

zh: 党的发展反映在党员增长上。1921年60万至70万党员中，90%是在内战期间招募的。尽管这些新党员中许多是狂热者，也有许多是可靠性可疑的机会主义者，而且几乎所有人都没有充分接受有关党的长期目标的思想教育。到1922年，约20万党员被“清洗”，在当时这意味着他们只是被开除出党；到1924年又有约20万人离开，总数剩下35万。同时，党大力招募新的、主要是无产阶级的党员，尤其是在1924年为纪念已故列宁而大规模吸收工人党员。额外的招募运动使党员人数到1929年即新经济政策最后一年达到109万。
这些新党员不是内战期间那种随机志愿者；相反，他们是由党自己挑选和审查的。而且，他们都受到充分的、日益简化和标准化的教义问答式马克思主义思想灌输；这种马克思主义在1924年后被称为马克思列宁主义。斯大林的《列宁主义问题》是阐述这一新信条的最著名文献。
en: The Party’s development is reflected in the growth of its membership. Ninety percent of the Party’s 600,000 to 700,000 members in 1921 had been recruited during the Civil War. Although many of these new members were zealots, many were also opportunists of dubious reliability, and almost all of them were poorly indoctrinated for the long-term purposes of the Party. By 1922 some 200,000 members had been “purged,” which in those days meant they were simply expelled from the Party; by 1924 around 200,000 more were gone, leaving a total of 350,000. At the same time, extensive efforts were made to recruit new and largely proletarian members, notably in the great “levy” of worker members in 1924 in honor of the late Lenin. Additional recruitment drives brought the Party’s membership to 1,090,000 in 1929, the last year of the NEP.

These new members were not random volunteers, as during the Civil War; rather, they had been selected and screened by the Party itself. Moreover, they were all well indoctrinated in an increasingly simplified and standardized, or catechized, version of Marxism that became known after 1924 as Marxism-Leninism. Stalin’s
is the best-known document setting forth this new creed.

zh: 尼基塔·赫鲁晓夫再次是这种新党人的好例子。整个内战期间，他在红军中担任初级政治委员；新经济政策开始时，他在矿业学院顿巴斯分院的“工人预科”（成人速成学校）接受了一定程度的教育。1924年，30岁的他成为当地党委书记，从而开始专职从事党的工作。1925年，他是第十四次党代表大会的候补代表，1927年成为第十五次代表大会有表决权的正式代表，这两次大会都忙于摧毁左派。有了上百万这样的新人，斯大林到1929年拥有的政治军队比列宁曾经拥有的任何军队都更稳固，一支准备在新领袖召唤下不经讨论或讨价还价就投入战斗的军队。
en: Nikita Khrushchev is once again a good example of this new Party man. After serving as a junior political commissar with the Red Army throughout the Civil War, at the beginning of the NEP he received something of an education at the “Workers’ Faculty” (adult crash schooling) of the Donbas branch of the Mining Institute. From there, in 1924 at the age of thirty he moved on to become the local Party secretary, thus entering full-time Party work. In 1925 he was an alternate delegate to the Fourteenth Party Congress, and in 1927 a full voting delegate to the Fifteenth Congress, both of which were occupied with destroying the Left. With a million such new men, Stalin by 1929 had a political army more solid than any Lenin ever possessed, one ready to do battle, without discussion or haggling, at the call of the new Leader.

zh: 因为自战时共产主义时代以来，党的内部组织已发生巨大变化。随着党规模扩大并成为一个行政机构，它形成了由专职机关干部组成的内部官僚体系，而普通党员则成为把党的路线传达到各职能行政机关和广大民众的传送带。这个内部官僚体系由从地方直到全联盟中央委员会的各级党“委员会”或执行机构组成。这个机构的常设执行机关是政治局，1921年后它成为国家的真正权力中心。但中央委员会也需要一个常设工作人员班子来管理新官僚体系；这就是书记处，列宁1922年让斯大林担任其首脑，即总书记。于是斯大林实际上成了党的人事官：他把党的工作者派到他认为需要的地方，只对政治局和中央委员会负责。在民主集中制下，党的工作者被派到哪里就去哪里。
en: For the internal organization of the Party had changed greatly since the days of War Communism. As the Party grew in size and became an administration, it acquired its own internal bureaucracy of full-time apparatchiki, whereas the ordinary members became transmission belts for bringing the Party’s line to the various functional administrations and the population at large. This internal bureaucracy consisted of a hierarchy of Party “committees,” or executive bodies, from the localities up to the All-Union Central Committee. The permanent executive organ of this body was the Politburo, which after 1921 became the real center of power in the country. But the Central Committee also needed a permanent staff to manage the new bureaucracy; this was the Secretariat, of which Lenin made Stalin the head, or General Secretary, in 1922. Stalin thus became, in effect, the personnel officer of the Party: He assigned Party workers where he deemed they were needed and was accountable only to the Politburo and the Central Committee. Under the regime of democratic centralism, Party workers went where they were told.

zh: 在实践中，这种人事管理方法意味着总书记可以任命下属地方委员会的书记，这些书记再选择党代表大会代表；而这些代表反过来重新选举斯大林为总书记。正是通过这种方式，他在1924年把托洛茨基挤出继承序列，然后在1925—1926年除掉了三驾马车同伴季诺维也夫和加米涅夫，最后在1927年粉碎了联合左派。对手相继被排除之后，到1928—1929年，他很容易转而对付布哈林及其盟友李可夫和托姆斯基，把他们作为“右倾偏离”排除出权力。于是到1929年大转折时，斯大林已成为党无可争议的主人。他还不是绝对独裁者，但他在党的结构内拥有绝对的发起议事的权力。
en: In practice this method of personnel management came to mean that the General Secretary could appoint the secretaries of subordinate local committees, who would then choose the delegates to Party congresses; in turn these delegates would reelect Stalin General Secretary. It was in this way that he had shouldered Trotsky out of the succession in 1924, and then disposed of his fellow triumvirs, Zinoviev and Kamenev, in 1925-1926, and finally crushed the United Left in 1927. With the field so narrowed, by 1928-1929 it was quite easy for him to turn on Bukharin and his allies, Rykov and Tomskii, and exclude them from power as the “Right deviation.” Thus by the Great Break of 1929 Stalin had become the unchallenged master of the Party. He was not yet an absolute dictator, but he had an absolute right of initiative within the Party structures.

children: 〔译注〕这里省略了中央委员会这一环节：党代会选举中央委员会，而中央委员会选举书记处。
〔译注〕这里省略了中央委员会这一环节：党代会选举中央委员会，而中央委员会选举书记处。

zh: 斯大林当然想要这种权力，正如他想成为列宁唯一的继承人。但主要用个人野心来解释他的崛起，是极其肤浅的。党的结构必须使他有可能形成自己的野心，而这些结构本身也呼唤着体现为一位领袖。单一的“正确”学说、被围困的心态、自上而下通过自上而下挑选补充成员的招募——所有这些加在一起，只能产生一个通过来自单一中心的命令运作的军事指挥组织。禁止派别使这一局面正式化，但并没有创造它。斯大林之所以能如此有效地消灭对手，是因为他比对手更理解党的真正性质。从1922年到1927年，当他们在辩论高层政策时，他关心的是控制党的机器。在这一努力中，他的手法与列宁1903年至1912年同孟什维克斗争时在俄国社会民主党内所用的手法完全一样。直到斯大林掌握了控制权，他才拿出自己的政策；在此期间，他支持布哈林的谨慎路线。
en: Stalin, of course, wanted this power, just as he wanted to be Lenin’s sole successor. But to explain his ascendancy essentially by personal ambition would be superficial in the extreme. Party structures had to make it possible for him to formulate his ambition, and these structures cried out for personification in one Leader. A single “correct” doctrine, an embattled siege mentality, and recruitment based on cooptation from the top down—all taken together could only produce a military command organization functioning through orders from a single center. The ban on factions formalized, but did not create, this situation. It was because Stalin understood the true nature of the Party better than his rivals that he was able to eliminate them so effectively. From 1922 to 1927, while they debated high policy, he concerned himself with getting control of the Party machine. And in this endeavor he maneuvered just as Lenin had done within the Russian Social Democratic Party in his struggle against the Mensheviks between 1903 and 1912. It was only once Stalin had control that he came out with his own policy; in the meantime he supported Bukharin’s cautious course.

zh: 但党的官僚化并不是斯大林成功的唯一关键；使他胜出的是党的意识形态统治性质，他也巧妙地利用了这一点。因为这个党不是普通政治团体，而是历史逻辑的载体，斯大林的所有对手都如此深信这一点，以至于在每一次危机中都自行缴械。正如托洛茨基1924年失败时所说：“党归根到底是永远正确的，因为党是给予无产阶级解决其根本问题的唯一历史工具……我知道，一个人不能
党而正确。一个人只能与党一起、通过党而正确，因为历史没有创造其他道路来实现正确的东西。”
面对这样的对手，斯大林几乎不需要盟友。而他所有的对手，无论“右派”还是“左派”，布哈林与季诺维也夫一样，都持同样想法。于是他们全都投降，承认自己的错误（唯一的例外是托洛茨基，1929年后他已没有认错的机会，因为他被逐出国外）。
en: But bureaucratization of the Party was not the only key to Stalin’s success; what put him over the top was the Party’s ideocratic nature, on which he also played adroitly. For this Party was no ordinary political body but the vehicle of the logic of history, and all of Stalin’s rivals believed this so deeply that they disarmed themselves before him in every crisis. As Trotsky said at the moment of his defeat in 1924: “The Party in the last analysis is always right, because the Party is the single historic instrument given to the proletariat for the solution of its fundamental problems … I know that one must not be right
the Party. One can only be right with the Party, and through the Party, for history has created no other road for the realization of what is right.”

With adversaries like this, Stalin hardly needed allies. And all his rivals, “Right” and “Left,” Bukharin no less than Zinoviev, thought the same. So they all capitulated and recanted their errors (with the sole exception of Trotsky, who after 1929 no longer had the option of recanting because he had been cast out of the country).

zh: 的确，他们后来都继续为新领袖服务，直到他在大清洗中将他们除掉。于是普列奥布拉任斯基、尤里·皮亚塔科夫和整个左派都为实施第一个五年计划效力，仿佛那是他们自己的计划。布哈林在计划集体化期间也尽职地保持沉默；他甚至写出了他自认为是新社会主义和自己生涯最高成就的1936年斯大林宪法，同年还在巴黎向一位流亡朋友自豪地展示那支历史性的钢笔。
因为对他和所有其他人来说，
（党性）比任何经济纲领或对农民的政策都更重要。
en: Indeed, they all went on to serve the new Leader until he cut them down in the Purges. Thus Preobrazhenskii, Iurii Piatakov, and all the Left worked for the First Five-Year Plan as if it were their own. And Bukharin dutifully fell silent during the Plan’s collectivization; he even penned what he considered to be the crowning achievement of both the new socialism and his own career, the Stalin Constitution of 1936, proudly exhibiting the historic pen to an émigré friend in Paris the same year.
For to him, as to all the others,
, or Party spirit, meant more than any economic program or policy towards the peasants.

zh: 此外，在二十年代过程中，这种精神从党本身扩展到了广大民众。正如我们所见，新经济政策年代常被描述为文化多元主义、先锋艺术和对希望中的社会主义未来大胆思辨的时期。
这确实是一个常有大胆社会实验的时期，有允许简易离婚和按需堕胎的激进立法，有现代主义或“进步”教育改革。
这也是一个非共产党人如果接受革命，就被党欢迎为创造新文化的“同路人”的时期。于是，在少数几年和少数领域里，俄国白银时代革命前的伟大繁荣得以延续。但总体而言，这十年的运动稳步朝相反方向前进：走向越来越大的意识形态一致性和国家对教育、文化及艺术日益加强的控制。
en: In the course of the 1920s, moreover, this spirit was extended from the Party itself to the population at large. The years of the NEP, as we have seen, have often been described as a period of cultural pluralism, of avant-garde art, and of audacious speculation about the hoped-for socialist future.
And it was indeed a period of often daring social experimentation, of radical legislation permitting easy divorce and abortion on demand, and of modernist or “progressive” educational reform.

31 It was also a time when non-Communists, if they accepted the Revolution, were welcomed by the Party as “fellow travellers” in creating the new culture. Thus, for a few years and in a few areas, there was a prolongation of the great prerevolutionary flowering of Russia’s Silver Age. Yet on the whole, the movement of the decade was steadily in the opposite direction: towards ever greater ideological conformity and state control over education, culture, and the arts.

zh: 首先，一切被认为敌视革命的文化潮流都受到积极打击。从孟什维主义到君主主义的各种政治思潮都被禁止。宗教成为战斗无神论者同盟发动的大规模迫害运动的目标。
更有甚者，党进行了一场史无前例的努力，向民众灌输单一的“正确”世界观；这一努力为这个时期赢得了“宣传国家的诞生”这一恰当称号。
en: To begin with, all cultural currents deemed hostile to the Revolution were actively combatted. All politics, from Menshevism to monarchism, were proscribed. Religion became the butt of a massive campaign of persecution conducted by the League of the Militant Godless.

What is more, the Party engaged in a historically unprecedented effort to indoctrinate the population in a single “correct” worldview, an effort that earned for the period the appropriate title “birth of the propaganda state.”

zh: 在这一过程中，马克思主义从政治知识分子的意识形态工具——他们试图理解世界以便改变世界，列宁和托洛茨基、普列奥布拉任斯基和布哈林就是这样使用马克思主义的——转变为由国家操纵、用来为其当下政策辩护的经院体系。斯大林“一国社会主义”的学说在这方面是过渡性的；它一半是对布尔什维克俄国孤立状态的分析，一半是在如此黯淡的局势中维系党内希望的手段。
en: In the course of this operation, Marxism was transformed from an ideological tool of political intellectuals seeking to understand their world so that they could change it—which is how Marxism was used by Lenin and Trotsky, or by Preobrazhenskii and Bukharin—into a scholastic system manipulated by the state to justify its policies of the moment. Stalin’s doctrine of “socialism in one country” is transitional in this respect; it was half an analysis of Bolshevik Russia’s isolation and half a means of fostering Party hope in such a bleak situation.

zh: 这样，现在被称为马克思列宁主义的词汇，被标准化和仪式化为所谓的“木语言”或“新语”。所有群体和个人都有固定标签，从贪婪的富农到背叛的小资产阶级，从帝国主义鲨鱼到英勇的突击工人：世界以摩尼教方式分为朋友和敌人，一切国内外时事都通过阶级斗争的棱镜折射。
en: Thus, the vocabulary of what was now called Marxism-Leninism was standardized and ritualized into what has variously been called “wooden language” or “newspeak.” All groups and individuals had their fixed labels, from greedy kulaks to traitorous petty bourgeois to imperialist sharks to valiant shock workers: The world was divided, in Manichean manner, into friends and enemies, and all current events, foreign and domestic, were refracted through the prism of the class struggle.

zh: 这些新范畴随后通过日报、新艺术电影以及很快传播更为广泛的广播媒介，反复灌入民众耳中。正如列宁谈到第一种媒介时所说：“报纸是集体的宣传员和集体的组织者。”于是这个国家被宣传鼓动淹没，既是为了推销当下的党的路线，也是为了动员民众为最终实现社会主义而努力。
en: These new categories were then dinned into the population through the daily press, the new art of the cinema, and soon the still more ubiquitous medium of radio. As Lenin said of the first of these media: “A newspaper is a collective agitator and a collective organizer.” And so the country was inundated by agitprop, both to put over the Party line of the moment and to mobilize the population for the eventual effort to achieve socialism.

zh: 在“文化”世界中，从未见过如此规模、如此彻底的东西。这种新语言也不只是装饰或修辞点缀。它对政权的权力至关重要。语言，如同生活中的一切，都必须为社会主义事业服务。事实上，语言比任何其他东西都更必须政治化，因为它既是社会动员的手段，也是影响民众意识的途径。因此，普通词语的含义必须被改变，以符合意识形态戒律。
en: Nothing on this scale, and nothing this total, had ever been seen before in the world of “culture.” Nor was this new language a mere ornament or rhetorical embellishment. It was essential to the power of the regime. Language, like everything else in life, had to be made to serve the cause of socialism. Indeed language, more than anything else, had to be politicized, since it was both the means of social mobilization and the way into the consciousness of the population. The meaning of ordinary words, accordingly, had to be altered to conform to ideological precepts.

zh: 因此，意识形态统治的党治也必然是一种话语统治；就此而言，它与如今铁板一块的制度的垄断结构完全一致。没有这种话语统治的魔咒，制度就无法运作：托洛茨基和布哈林不可能相信一个人不可能在反对党的同时保持正确；斯大林也不可能使对手屈从于他的总路线，冲进大转折。
en: The ideocratic partocracy, therefore, was also necessarily logocratic; and as such it was of a piece with the monopolistic structure of the now monolithic system. Without this logocratic spell, the system could not function: Trotsky and Bukharin could not have believed that it was impossible to be right against the Party; and Stalin could riot have bent his opponents to follow his General Line and rush into the Great Break.

zh: 因此，在政治上——随着党机关的发展——和文化上——随着新语的兴起——新经济政策时期的发展路线并不通向自由化，而是通向斯大林时期三十年代实际出现的局面。
en: Thus politically—with the growth of the Party apparat—and culturally—with the rise of newspeak—the line of development during the NEP did not lead to liberalization, but to where matters actually wound up under Stalin in the thirties.

zh: 只有在这种政治和文化背景下，才能回答关于“布哈林替代方案”可行性的社会主义反事实问题。或者，反过来，用一篇关于苏联历史这一核心问题的著名文章的术语来说：斯大林是否真的必要？
en: It is only against this political and cultural background that it is possible to answer the socialist counterfactual question of the feasibility of the “Bukharin alternative.” Or, to put the matter the other way around, and in the terms of a famous essay on this central issue of Soviet history: Was Stalin really necessary?

zh: 然而，无论问题怎样提，答案都可能是或否，取决于人们认为布哈林替代方案意味着什么。如果把它理解为一个基本上旨在使俄国成为发达国家的经济纲领——这常被视为它的本质——那么布哈林那种由国家指导、但保留市场的经济公式本会产生可观的结果，而且人的代价远低于斯大林纲领。事实上，此后韩国、台湾和巴西等地常常实行大致类似的混合经济版本。
en: Yet whichever way the question is put, the answer can be either yes or no, depending on what one considers Bukharin’s alternative to mean. If it is understood to be basically an economic program designed to make Russia a developed country—and this is what is frequently taken to be its essence—then Bukharin’s formula of a state-guided yet market economy would have produced respectable results, and at far less human cost than Stalin’s program. In fact, roughly comparable versions of a mixed economy have often been followed since then in such places as South Korea, Taiwan, and Brazil.

zh: 但这不是布哈林本人以其名字命名的替代方案所指。他指的是向完整或整体社会主义的过渡，而且是在党的政治垄断下实现。他也没有真正想清楚过渡的细节。他“通过市场长入社会主义”的战略需要大量时间，大约十年或更久，而在现有新经济政策下粮食采购逐月下降。党的革命热情能支撑一场通向目标的漫长过渡吗？此外，布哈林的战略需要两项他几乎没有暗示的让步：第一，建立真正的农民苏维埃，使工农联盟中的乡村一方对苏维埃国家有某种信心；第二，在允许正常利润的条件下，向外国资本部分开放国门，以使俄国度过新经济政策管理不善已使她陷入的危机。
en: But this is not what Bukharin himself meant by the alternative that bears his name. He meant, rather, a transition to full or integral socialism, to be achieved, moreover, under the political monopoly of the Party. Nor had he really thought out the details of the transition. His strategy of “growing into socialism through the market” would have required a great deal of time, on the order of a decade or more, and grain procurements under existing NEP policies were declining by the month. Would the Party’s revolutionary zeal have held up for a long transition to its goal? Bukharin’s strategy, moreover, would have required two concessions that he barely hinted at: first, real peasant soviets to give the rural half of the

some measure of confidence in the Soviet state; and second, partially opening the country to foreign capital on terms permitting normal profit, in order to get Russia through the crisis into which mismanagement of the NEP had already plunged her.

zh: 但这两项让步都意味着突破党的权力垄断，换句话说，攻击党存在的根本理由——或者用党如今已磨炼得很好的话语统治习语来说，就是在国内向“富农小资产阶级”投降，在国外向“帝国主义”投降。因此，在1928—1929年危机中，控制着扩大后的党机器的人迅速得出结论：他们没有时间等上几年、甚至好几个月来解决农民“怠工”问题，因为党的目标——建设社会主义——已随计划开始实现。对党来说，新经济政策从来不是一项“发展经济学”实践；它只是走向社会主义的一种战略。一旦新经济政策妨碍这一目标，就该抛弃它了。
en: But both of these concessions would have meant breaching the Party’s monopoly of power, in other words, attacking the Party’s very raison d’être—or, as the Party’s now well-honed logocratic idiom put it, capitulating to the “kulak petty bourgeoisie” internally and to “imperialism” externally. Thus, in the crisis of 1928-1929 the men who controlled the expanded Party machine swiftly concluded that they did not have time to wait years, or even many months, for a solution to peasant “sabotage,” because the realization of the Party’s goal, building socialism, was already under way with the Plan. For the Party, the NEP was never an exercise in “development economics”; rather, it was simply a strategy for moving towards socialism. And once the NEP got in the way of this goal, it was time to discard it.

zh: 从这个视角看，关于布哈林替代方案可行性的最终答案必须是否定的。鉴于其性质，指望列宁主义政党在危机压力下向它被创造出来要消灭的阶级敌人投降，是完全不可信的。同样，党的领导权落到斯大林和其他内战政委——莫洛托夫、卡冈诺维奇、伏罗希洛夫、奥尔忠尼启则、基洛夫和安德烈耶夫——这类人手中，也绝非偶然；这些人现在主导着政治局。在新经济政策危机中，这样的党和这样的领袖只能作出政治决定而非经济决定——更准确地说，是作出政治—军事决定（我们必须这样称呼他们回归战时共产主义强制方法的做法）来实施集体化。
en: In this perspective, the final answer to the question of the Bukharin alternative’s feasibility must be negative. Given its nature, it was wholly implausible to expect the Leninist Party to capitulate, under pressure of a crisis, to the class enemies it had been created to destroy. Similarly, it was no accident that the Party’s leadership had fallen into the hands of men like Stalin and the other Civil War commissars—Molotov, Kaganovich, Voroshilov, Ordzhonikidze, Kirov, and Andreev—who now dominated the Politburo. In the crisis of the NEP, such a party and such leaders could only be expected to make a political rather than an economic decision—or more exactly, to make a political-military decision (as we must call their reversion to the coercive methods of War Communism) to carry out collectivization.

zh: 因此，鉴于布哈林本人接受的党霸权原则，他的替代方案过于狭隘地局限于经济，无法在党的生存危机中获胜。相反，斯大林选择军事化政治的优先地位，完全符合基本列宁主义。因为列宁主义的本质从来不是某一种经济纲领；它始终是党作为历史实现社会主义的唯一工具，以武装手段夺取并维持权力垄断。把列宁主义误认为某种“经济主义”或近乎孟什维主义，是布哈林在二十年代的重大错误，此后也一直是他追随者的错误。对布尔什维克党来说，1929年的真正选择不是斯大林道路还是布哈林道路，而是大致做斯大林所做的事，还是放弃整个列宁主义事业。
en: Thus, given the principle of Party hegemony Bukharin himself accepted, his alternative was too narrowly economic to prevail in a crisis of Party survival. Conversely, Stalin’s option for the primacy of militarized politics was quite in accord with basic Leninism. For the essence of Leninism had never been one or another economic program; it had always been the armed seizure and preservation of a monopoly of power for the Party as history’s only vessel for achieving socialism. Mistaking Leninism for some kind of “economism,” or near-Menshevism, was Bukharin’s great error in the twenties, as it has been that of his votaries ever since. For a Bolshevik Party the real choice in 1929 was not between Stalin’s road and Bukharin’s; it was between doing approximately what Stalin did and giving up the whole Leninist enterprise.

zh: 无疑会有人反对说，这种推理是“决定论的”，使斯大林的选择显得不可避免或必然。事实上完全不是这样：这是一个“如果—那么”论证，主张一旦列宁主义政党掌权，此后一大批选项就被排除，只剩下另一个更狭窄的范围是可能或可行的。因此十月之后，市场和私有财产在结构上被“排除”，而党国的“命令—行政”方法——戈尔巴乔夫时期反对派这样称呼——在结构上被“纳入”。布哈林替代方案朝十月已经排除的方向走得太远，不可能是真正布尔什维主义的长期道路。于是党在新经济政策摧毁党本身之前提前结束新经济政策，回到战时共产主义的第一条路线。
en: It will no doubt be objected that this reasoning is “deterministic” and makes Stalin’s choice appear inevitable or necessary. In fact, it is nothing of the sort: It is an “if-then” argument that holds that once a Leninist Party comes to power, a whole range of options is thereafter excluded, leaving only another, narrower range as possible or feasible. Thus after October the market and private property were structurally “out,” and Party-state “command-administrative” methods, as they came to be called by the opposition under Gorbachev, were structurally “in.” The Bukharin alternative went too far towards what October had already excluded to be the long-term road for true Bolshevism. So the Party cut the NEP short before it destroyed the Party itself, and returned to its first course of War Communism.

zh: 不过，新经济政策确实留下了一份持久遗产：它成为党最初基本纲领的永久替代方案，每当一轮战时共产主义把国家的人员与物质基础推到崩溃点，这个替代方案就会重新浮现。这样，到1929年，苏联历史已划定其基本模式：在“硬”共产主义与“软”共产主义之间交替，在完整的非资本主义与被迫同根深蒂固的“阶级”敌人——也就是现实——妥协之间交替。这一模式使“苏联历史戏剧成为一出两幕剧，用不同的布景和人物反复上演”。
直到最后一场新经济政策——
——之后，整个破旧演出落幕为止，情况一直如此。
en: Still, the NEP did leave an enduring residue: It became the permanent alternative to the Party’s first and basic program, an alternative that would resurface each time a bout of War Communism pushed the human and material fabric of the country to the breaking point. In this way, by 1929 Soviet history had staked out its fundamental pattern of alternating between “hard” and “soft” Communism, between full noncapitalism and forced compromise with the inveterate “class” enemy—that is, with reality. This pattern made “the Soviet historical drama a two-act play, replayed several times with different sets and characters.”
And so it remained until the final curtain came down on the whole threadbare show after the last NEP—

zh: 然而在1929年，列宁的党仍处于革命活力的顶峰，于是最宏伟的一幕拉开了帷幕——通过斯大林的五年计划建设社会主义。这一次，不达目标绝不回头，绝不同阶级敌人妥协。最后那些怨声不止的反对派将被扫到一边，如今已臻完善的党军，在一位新的“今日列宁”率领下，将高呼“没有布尔什维克攻不下的堡垒”前进。
en: Yet in 1929 the Party of Lenin was still at the peak of its revolutionary vigor, so the curtain went up on the grandest act of all—the building of socialism through Stalin’s Five-Year Plan. This time there would be no turning back short of the goal, no compromises with the class enemy. The last, whining opposition would be swept aside, and the now perfected Party army, led by a new “Lenin for today,” would march forth under the slogan “there are no fortresses that Bolsheviks cannot storm.”
